Layouts.line: The container defining the installation's physical light topology.
Layouts.summary: One `Layouts` describes the setup, and every layer in `Effects` renders into it. Children stitch into one flat physical address space, in registration order.

guide.title: Order and universes
guide.text: Disabling a layout removes its lights and the layouts after it shift down. Reordering by drag and drop shifts them too. Both move Art-Net universe assignments, so disable the driver to keep a mapping stable.

guide.title: The status line
guide.text: It reports the total light count and the physical bounding box. A dense grid's count equals its box volume, so a smaller count signals a sparse layout.

Effects.line: The container holding every rendering layer, which `Drivers` composites into one output.
Effects.summary: Each layer renders independently into its own buffer, over the physical topology the shared `Layouts` describes.

Layer.line: One rendering layer: a buffer, a mapping onto physical lights, and the effects that fill it.
Layer.summary: Effects write the buffer, modifiers reshape it, and `Drivers` composites the stack of layers into one output.

guide.title: Trails and fades
guide.text: Nothing clears the buffer between frames, so an effect that fades what is already there leaves a trail. A fade is a rate, so a trail is the same length at any frame rate. Several fading effects cost one pass.

guide.title: The status line
guide.text: The status shows the logical box the effects render into. A mirror modifier folds a 128 by 128 layout into a 64 by 64 box. A warning replaces it when the layer does not fit in memory.

blendMode.line: How this layer combines with the layers below it.
blendMode.more: Multiply darkens what is beneath it, additive adds light, and alpha blends by opacity.

opacity.line: How strongly this layer shows, from invisible to full.

Drivers.line: The container of driver modules, owning the shared buffer and the per-light output correction every driver applies before sending.
Drivers.summary: Every driver under it reads its own slice of that buffer, as the [drivers catalog](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html) shows.

on.more: Off scales the output to black and keeps `brightness`, so switching on restores the level. The UI, infrared, the WLED app, Home Assistant and MQTT all drive it.

relayPins.line: GPIOs switching the LED power supply, closed while `on` and brightness is above 0.

brightness.line: Global output brightness, multiplied with each driver's `localBrightness`.
brightness.more: It starts low, so a fresh device on USB 5 V never browns out at full white.

tests.title: Control a palette preset changes only the palette

palette.line: What effects sample from: a built-in palette or a scripted `.mlp` one.

tests.title: Control a palette preset changes only the palette
Palettes a script drives the effects

paletteScript.line: The scripted palette's file, which `palette` picks.

tests.title: Palettes a script drives the effects

motionHold.line: How long a powered-off rig keeps tracking before its heads go still, in seconds.
motionHold.more: A short hold is a blackout between cues, a long one a park between sets.

multicore.line: Run the output stage on the second core.
multicore.more: It falls back to one core by itself when the extra frame buffer does not fit. The switch exists to compare the two.

renderWait.line: How long core 0 waited for core 1 at the frame boundary.
renderWait.more: Near zero means render and output overlap well. A large value means core 0 idles on a slow output stage.

FixtureProfilesModule.line: The named channel wirings drivers reference: which channel carries Red, Green, Blue, White, or a fixture role such as Pan and Tilt.
FixtureProfilesModule.summary: Real fixtures ship read-only, the color orders, multi-channel pars and moving heads. Add your own alongside them. A driver saves its profile by name, so a rename sends it back to its default at the next boot.

guide.title: 16-bit channels
guide.text: A fine role is the low byte of a 16-bit channel, the DMX convention. `RGB 16-bit`, `GRB 16-bit` and `RGBW 16-bit` ship built in. Effects stay 8-bit, and brightness and curve go to 16 bits on output. Pan and tilt widen by repeating their byte, and a master dimmer is held wide open.

guide.title: Which profile a chip takes
guide.text:
| Chip | Profile |
|---|---|
| WS2812B, WS2813, WS2815 | `GRB` |
| SK6812 RGBW | `GRBW` |
| WS2814 | `WRGB` |
| WS2816 | `GRB 16-bit` |
| UCS8903 | `RGB 16-bit` |
| UCS8904 | `RGBW 16-bit` |

A WS2811 orders its colors as its maker wired it, so try `RGB`, then the other five orders. The TM1814 and TM1914 need a settings preamble that a profile cannot describe.

profiles.line: The editable list of profile rows.
profiles.more: A row carries a name, a channel count and one role picker per channel. Built-in rows are read-only, and custom rows persist across a reboot.

CarLightsLayout.line: A pair of car headlights: concentric rings of lights placed like a car's front lamps.
CarLightsLayout.summary: Nested rings of 1, 8, 12, 16 and 24 lights form each lamp, with a ring of 32 more on the outer two. Side strips join them, in a fixed arrangement drawn with [Ring](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/layouts.html#ring) geometry.

scale.line: The overall size: the spacing out from each lamp's center.

CubeLayout.line: A solid 3D cube of lights, wired through the volume in the axis order you choose.
CubeLayout.summary: Every point of a `width` × `height` × `depth` box holds a light. The strip's path is yours to set: which axis it runs along first, which way each axis counts, and which axes snake back and forth. It is the 3D form of [Panel](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/layouts.html#panel).

wiringOrder.line: The axis order the strip follows, fastest first.

X++.line: Whether x counts up rather than down.

snakeX.line: Whether x snakes, reversing on alternate passes.

HumanSizedCubeLayout.line: A walk-in cube of five LED curtains: front, back, top, left and right, open at the bottom.
HumanSizedCubeLayout.summary: Each face is a curtain the size of the box's side, for a room-scale cube a person stands inside.

MoonLiveLayout.line: Where the lights physically are, written as text on the running device.
MoonLiveLayout.summary: A layout is the one part of the pipeline that differs for every build: a ring, a spiral staircase, a costume sewn last night. A script means the person who hung the lights describes where they went, and sees it at once. Everything the script declares appears as a real control. The language is [MoonLive](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/moonlive.html).

guide.title: How the light count is known
guide.text: The Layer sizes its buffer from the light count before it asks for any position, so the script runs twice: the first pass counts `addLight` calls, the second emits positions. Nothing is stored between passes, which saves 48 KB at 16,384 lights. A `random16` loop bound makes the passes disagree on the count.

guide.title: What a layout script is given
guide.text: `addLight(x, y, z)` places the next light, in call order. `t` is always 0 and `width`, `height` and `depth` read 0, since a layout is upstream of the grid. Name your own size controls, such as `cols` and `rows`. [The MoonLive guide](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/moonlive.html#system-variables) lists the vocabulary.

script.line: Which `.mll` script runs, picked from the library and edited here.

PanelsLayout.line: An M × N grid of matrix panels, tiled into one large display for a video wall.
PanelsLayout.summary: The wiring is two walks, each set on its own: an outer one over the panel grid and an inner one over each panel's lights, as [Panel](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/layouts.html#panel) wires one.

wiringOrderP.line: Which axis the panel grid walks first.

X++P.line: Whether the panel grid's x counts up.

snakeP.line: Serpentine across the panel grid: alternate panel rows run in reverse.

wiringOrder.line: Which axis a panel walks first.

X++.line: Whether a panel's x counts up.

snake.line: Serpentine inside each panel: alternate lines run in reverse.

TorontoBarGourdsLayout.line: A bar's installation of 24 decorative gourds, each lit at one of three granularities: one light per gourd, per side, or per LED.

granularity.line: How finely each gourd is lit.
granularity.more: One gourd one light stacks its lights on one position. One side one light gives each of five sides a point. One LED one light places each LED on its side's ring of 12.

nrOfLightsPerGourd.line: Lights per gourd when one gourd is one light.

GridLayout.line: A dense grid of lights in 1D, 2D or 3D: every position holds a light, wired row by row.
GridLayout.summary: The wiring runs x fastest, then y, then z, and a strip that snakes back and forth runs every other row in reverse.

tests.title: Effects teardown under a running pipeline

depth.line: Its extent on z, 1 for a flat panel.

serpentine.line: Every other row runs in reverse, for a snaked strip.

GridBlacksLayout.line: A grid with dark columns held black in every row, for a sealed panel that must stay dark down a strip, or a slat wall.
GridBlacksLayout.summary: A dark column is still a wire position the driver clocks, so data flows through the unlit lights to the lit columns beyond. The lit columns keep their true positions, so an effect maps straight across the gap. Without dark columns it is a [Grid](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/layouts.html#grid).

serpentine.line: Every other row runs in reverse, matching a snaked strip.

blackCount.line: How many dark columns; none renders exactly like a Grid.

PanelLayout.line: A 2D matrix panel with full wiring control: the axis order, the direction per axis, and serpentine.
PanelLayout.summary: The general matrix layout, of which [Grid](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/layouts.html#grid) is the simple case.

X++.line: Whether x counts up rather than down.

snake.line: Serpentine wiring: alternate lines run in reverse.

RingLayout.line: A ring of lights evenly spaced around a circle, or an arc of one.
RingLayout.summary: The lights start at `angleFirst` and span `rotation` degrees, a full turn drawing the whole circle. A center of its own places the ring anywhere, which is how CarLights and Rings241 build their lamps and discs from rings.

nrOfLEDs.line: How many lights go around the ring.

angleFirst.line: The angle the first light sits at, in degrees.

rotation.line: The arc spanned in degrees, less than a full turn a partial ring.

scale.line: The spacing out from the center.

centerX.line: The center's x before scaling; 0 places the ring by its size.

centerY.line: The center's y before scaling; 0 places the ring by its size.

Rings241Layout.line: The classic 241-light disc: nine concentric rings of 1, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48 and 60 lights sharing a center.

scale.line: The size: scales the ring radii and the shared center.

outside in.line: Light 0 on the outer ring, wired inward rather than outward.
outside in.more: A disc is soldered from its center or from its 60-light rim, and this follows the end the data enters. Each ring keeps the direction it is wired in.

angleFirst.line: The angle light 0 of each ring sits at, in degrees.

SingleColumnLayout.line: A vertical line of lights at a fixed x, the 1D column.

starting Y.line: The row the column starts at.

height.line: How many lights the column holds.

reversed order.line: Wire it top to bottom rather than bottom to top.

SingleRowLayout.line: A horizontal line of lights at a fixed y: the 1D row, a bare strip laid straight.

starting X.line: The column the row starts at.

width.line: How many lights the row holds.

reversed order.line: Wire it right to left rather than left to right.

SphereLayout.line: Lights on the surface of a hollow sphere: a shell one light thick, nothing inside.

SpiralLayout.line: A conical spiral: lights winding up a cone from a wide base to a point.

ledCount.line: How many lights wind up the spiral.

bottomRadius.line: The radius at the base, in light-units.

height.line: The vertical rise from base to tip.

TubesLayout.line: Parallel vertical tubes, each a column of lights, standing side by side.

nrOfTubes.line: How many tubes stand side by side.

ledsPerTube.line: How many lights each tube carries.

tubeDistance.line: The spacing between tubes, in light-units.

reversed.line: Wire each tube from its top.

WheelLayout.line: A bicycle wheel: spokes radiating from a center hub, each a straight row of lights.

spokes.line: How many spokes radiate from the hub.

ledsPerSpoke.line: How many lights each spoke carries.

AudioSpectrumEffect.line: The 16 mic frequency bands spread across X, each column lit bottom-up by its magnitude.
AudioSpectrumEffect.summary: The classic equalizer display. The bands scale to any width, so a wide grid gives each several columns and a narrow one samples. On a grid at least three rows tall, the bottom row becomes a horizontal level bar and the spectrum bars sit above it. On a single row the bars collapse to per-column brightness.

colorMode.line: Bars colored by height, the VU look, or per band, a rainbow.

tests.title: Effects teardown under a running pipeline

RadialSpectrumEffect.line: The spectrum as ripples: each band owns a sector around the center, mirrored left and right with the bass at top and bottom.
RadialSpectrumEffect.summary: Sound is born at the center and travels outward, so the radius is time and a ring's length is that band's recent history. On a cube the ripples are expanding shells. `polarTable`, `polarTable16` and `mapping` set the polar address and its shape.

speed.line: How fast sound travels outward.

persistence.line: How far out a ripple stays visible.

smooth.line: Read the meter ballistic rather than the raw bands.

beat.line: A white shockwave born at the center on every onset.

VuMetersEffect.line: Sixteen needles, one per band, each with real mass.
VuMetersEffect.summary:
What makes a VU meter beautiful is the needle: it overshoots a peak, swings back and settles. That is why a mechanical meter reads as alive where a bar graph reads as a readout.

The bass needles are heavier than the treble ones, so the low end swings and the high end flickers.

damping.line: How much the needle overshoots: low swings, high settles.

response.line: How quickly the needle chases the signal at all.

peakHold.line: How long the peak marker stays up.

smooth.line: Drive from the smoothed ballistic rather than the raw band.

BeatRipplesEffect.line: Every beat is a stone dropped in water.
BeatRipplesEffect.summary: A real wave simulation, which gives what a drawn expanding circle cannot: ripples pass through each other, reflect off the walls and interfere into standing patterns. The loudest band decides where the stone lands, a bass hit near the center and a treble hit out at the rim, and its strength sets how deep.

damping.line: How long the water keeps ringing.

drop.line: How deep a beat's stone falls.

rain.line: Idle drops when there is no music, so the surface is alive in silence.

shine.line: How strongly the slope lights the surface.

BlurzEffect.line: Audio-reactive blurred dots: one frequency band per frame lights a dot, then the whole frame is blurred for soft trails.
BlurzEffect.summary: The dot's position maps to that band, or to the major-peak frequency with `freqMap`. `geqScanner` sweeps the dot steadily across the strip, and with neither the dot jumps to a random position.

freqMap.line: Place the dot by the major-peak frequency, not by scanning.

geqScanner.line: Scan the dot across the strip in a GEQ-like sweep.

BouncingBallsEffect.line: A row of balls per column bounce under gravity, each losing energy on impact and relaunching when it stops.
BouncingBallsEffect.summary: Every column runs independently, so a panel shows a forest of bouncing dots, palette-colored by ball index over a fading background.

grav.line: Gravity strength: higher falls faster and bounces snappier.

DemoReelEffect.line: Plays every other registered effect in turn, auto-advancing on a timer, so one Layer cycles the whole library hands-free.
DemoReelEffect.summary: New effects are picked up automatically. It can pick a fresh palette each cycle and overlay the playing effect's name, and the status line says which is playing. It never hosts itself, and it plays in sequence rather than compositing.

interval.line: Seconds each effect plays before advancing.

shuffle.line: Jump to a random next effect instead of registry order.

randomPalette.line: Pick a random palette on each cycle.

showName.line: Overlay the playing effect's name in a small font.

DistortionWavesEffect.line: Two interfering sine waves beat against each other into a moire color field.
DistortionWavesEffect.summary: The waves run at independent frequencies and slightly different time rates, and their summed value indexes the active palette.

speed.line: Animation rate; 0 freezes it.

FireEffect.line: A Fire2012-style heat field: sparks at the base rise and cool through the active palette, coldest at its low end.
FireEffect.summary: The spark count scales with the width. The flame color comes from the active palette: the Lava palette (black, red, orange, yellow, white) gives the classic fire. An Ocean or Forest palette turns the flame blue or green.

cooling.line: How fast heat dissipates as it rises; higher is shorter flames.

sparking.line: Chance of a new spark at the base each frame; higher is livelier.

FixedRectangleEffect.line: A solid color filling a positioned box within the grid, with an optional alternating-white checker on the box's pixels.
FixedRectangleEffect.summary: A box at a dialed-in position and extent over a slow motion-trail fade, so it serves as a static fixture, an alignment aid, or a painted region. An extent beyond the grid fills to the edge.

white.line: The box color, white, on an RGBW grid.

X position.line: The box's origin corner on x.

Y position.line: The box's origin corner on y.

Z position.line: The box's origin corner on z.

alternateWhite.line: Alternate box pixels to white in a checker pattern.

FreqMatrixEffect.line: A 1D scrolling frequency display: each frame shifts the strip and injects a new pixel at one end.
FreqMatrixEffect.summary: The new pixel's hue comes from the dominant frequency and its brightness from the volume, so pitch becomes color.

speed.line: Scroll rate.

fx.line: Sound-effect intensity, scaling the injected brightness.

lowBin.line: The lower edge of the frequency window mapped across the hue range.

highBin.line: The upper edge of that window.

audioSpeed.line: Let the volume modulate the scroll speed.

FreqSawsEffect.line: Audio-reactive sawtooth waves: each column maps to a frequency band whose loudness drives a per-band oscillator speed.
FreqSawsEffect.summary: Louder bands sweep their sawtooth up the column faster. A band's speed rises instantly to a loud hit and decays slowly once the sound stops. A struck band keeps sawing for a while, and a quiet one winds down.

fade.line: Background decay per frame, which is the motion trail.

increaser.line: How fast a band's speed ramps up with its magnitude.

decreaser.line: How fast a silent band's speed decays.

bpmMax.line: Ceiling on a band's oscillation speed.

invert.line: Flip alternate columns vertically, for a woven look.

keepOn.line: Keep oscillating even when a band is silent.

method.line: The phase model that places the saw.
method.more: `Chaos` reads the position off the beat, so the saw teleports as the rate changes. `Chaos fix` carries a per-band offset, so a rate change continues smoothly. `BandPhases` integrates an accumulator, so the saw never jumps.

FseqPlayerEffect.line: Plays FSEQ animation files from the filesystem onto this effect's layer, with a playlist and the standard transport controls.
FseqPlayerEffect.summary: FSEQ is the Falcon Player/xLights sequence format: a flat, per-frame byte stream with no pixel semantics of its own. The playlist follows `FixtureProfilesModule`'s `EditableListSource` shape, the transport `DemoReelEffect`'s cycle/shuffle logic.

guide.title: Compressed files need ESP32
guide.text:
A zlib-compressed FSEQ (xLights/FPP's default) plays only on ESP32 boards; desktop and Teensy builds show a clean error instead of playing it.

Zstd-compressed files do not play on any target yet.

Export a track uncompressed if it needs to play everywhere.

play.line: Starts a stopped transport, or resumes a paused one.

pause.line: Holds the current frame on screen.

stop.line: Stops playback, resets the position and blanks the lights.

previous.line: Jumps to the previous track in the playlist.

next.line: Jumps to the next track in the playlist.

shuffle.line: Picks the next track at random instead of in playlist order.

loopMode.line: At a track's end: stop, repeat it, or repeat the playlist.

fpsSource.line: where the rate comes from: the file's step time, or fps_

fps.line: the manual playback rate; 1000/fps milliseconds per frame

playlist.line: The tracks to play, in order; each row picks a scanned .fseq file.

position.line: How far into the current track playback is, in frames.

rescan.line: Looks through the filesystem for .fseq files again.

GameOfLifeEffect.line: Conway's cellular automaton generalized to 2D and 3D, with selectable rulesets and a custom `B#/S#` rule.
GameOfLifeEffect.summary: Cells live, die and are born by counting their live neighbors, on a panel or through a cube. New cells take a neighbor's palette color, and dead ones blur toward the background.

guide.title: Reading a rule
guide.text: A rule lists the neighbor counts that give birth (B) and let a cell survive (S): Conway's `B3/S23` is born at 3, survives at 2 or 3. HighLife `B36/S23` breeds replicators, Maze `B3/S12345` grows corridors. `Custom B/S` takes `customRuleString` as `36/23`.

guide.title: A board that never ends
guide.text: With `infinite` on, a board that dies out, repeats itself or thins below a twentieth gets a new R-pentomino or glider dropped in, so the show keeps going. Off, it pauses a moment and starts a fresh game, as `startingLifeDensity` fills it.

backgroundColorR.line: The background's red channel, which dead cells fade toward.

ruleset.line: The birth and survive rule, from Conway's to Maze, or your own.

customRuleString.line: Your own rule: birth digits, a slash, survive digits.

startingLifeDensity.line: Percent of cells alive at the start.

mutationChance.line: Percent chance a newborn gets a random color.

wrap.line: Toroidal edges on a 2D board; a lone glider and a cube run off.

disablePause.line: Skip the 1.5 second settle pause between boards.

colorByAge.line: Age cells from green to red, not a neighbor's palette color.

infinite.line: Respawn a pentomino or glider on stasis instead of resetting.

blur.line: Dead-cell fade strength toward the background color.

GEQEffect.line: A flat graphic equalizer: the 16 audio bands rise as vertical bars from the bottom.
GEQEffect.summary: The bands spread across the columns, each rising to its loudness, with optional smoothing, per-bar palette coloring and falling peak markers. A peak dot sits at the highest the bar recently reached and falls back slowly. [GEQ3D](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/effects.html#geq3d) draws the same data in perspective.

fadeOut.line: How fast bars fade each frame, which is the motion trail.

ripple.line: Falling-peak marker decay; 0 removes the marker.

colorBars.line: Color each bar from the palette by band instead of by row.

smoothBars.line: Blend neighboring bands for smoother bar heights.

GEQ3DEffect.line: A 3D-perspective graphic equalizer: audio bands rise as bars with faked depth.
GEQ3DEffect.summary: Side and top lines run toward a "projector" vanishing point that sweeps left and right, shortened by `depth`. Bands left of it paint right-to-left and bands right of it left-to-right, with per-face darkening and optional `borders`. [GEQ](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/effects.html#geq) draws the same data flat.

speed.line: How fast the projector sweeps, the same position on every device.

frontFill.line: How strongly a bar's front face fills.

horizon.line: The row the vanishing point (the projector) sits on.

depth.line: How far the side and top lines reach toward the projector.

numBands.line: How many bands are shown, where fewer gives wider bars.

LavaLampEffect.line: Three slow metaball blobs that rise and merge, colored by the active palette.
LavaLampEffect.summary: The blobs' summed field indexes the palette, so the lamp takes its colors and a palette dark at its low end keeps the gaps dark. Its sibling [Metaballs](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/effects.html#metaballs) runs the same field fast and in HSV.

intensity.line: Field gain into the palette, which is what merges the blobs.

LinesEffect.line: Axis-aligned planes sweep in sync, where red, green and blue name the x, y and z axis.
LinesEffect.summary: A test pattern for verifying a preview's axis orientation. The `lines` mode sweeps a plane along each axis, and the `panel dots` mode shows a static panel-mapping aid where each panel lights one more dot than the last.

mode.line: Sweep the planes, or show the static panel dots.

speed.line: Sweep speed in BPM, in `lines` mode.

axis.line: Which plane sweeps: all, x, y or z, in `lines` mode.

panelW.line: The panel width the dots walk, in `panel dots` mode.

panelH.line: The panel height the dots walk, in `panel dots` mode.

LissajousEffect.line: A Lissajous curve traced across the grid, palette-colored along its length, with a fading trail.
LissajousEffect.summary: Sample points sweep an x and a y oscillator whose frequencies and shared phase drift, so the closed curve continuously morphs and rotates.

xFrequency.line: The x-axis sweep frequency, which sets the curve's lobe count.

fadeRate.line: How fast the trail fades each frame.

speed.line: How fast the curve's phase advances.

MetaballsEffect.line: Blobs orbit and merge smoothly, where the summed field of all balls picks each pixel's color and brightness.
MetaballsEffect.summary: Each ball contributes a field that falls off with distance, and the sum picks the color. Where two balls approach, their fields add and the blobs appear to merge. [LavaLamp](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/effects.html#lavalamp) runs the same field slowly through a palette instead.

radius.line: How far each blob's influence reaches.

MoonLiveEffect.line: An effect written as text on the running device, compiled to native code on the next tick.
MoonLiveEffect.summary: Pick a script from the library or write your own, and it renders at the speed of a compiled effect. Every control the script declares appears on the card and is editable live without a recompile. The language is [MoonLive](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/moonlive.html).

script.line: Which `.mle` script runs, picked from the library and edited here.

NetworkReceiveEffect.line: Receives lights over UDP into the layer, from Resolume, Madrix, xLights and LedFx.
NetworkReceiveEffect.summary: It listens for Art-Net, E1.31 and DDP at once, with no protocol control, so whatever a sender speaks works and the status names it. The received lights land in the layer buffer, so they compose with modifiers and blending.

universe_start.line: The first incoming universe to map, mirroring the sender.

channels_per_universe.line: Bytes each universe maps to, 510 or 512.

mapped_by.line: Whether the sender or the receiver maps the frame onto the wiring.
mapped_by.more: **receiver**: frames arrive row by row and this board applies its wiring. **sender**: a [NetworkSend](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html#networksend) sends wiring order, keeping byte order, brightness 255 and the linear curve.

packets_per_s.line: Packets received in the last second, read-only.

frames_per_s.line: Frames received in the last second, read-only.

NoiseEffect.line: A gradient-noise field indexed straight into the palette, the plainest way to turn noise into light.
NoiseEffect.summary: It is the effect every other noise effect is a variation on. The `motion` control decides what moves, which is the whole character of the effect.

motion.line: Whether the field drifts across the fixture or morphs in place.
motion.more: `drift` slides the field across the fixture like weather, each axis at its own rate. `morph` holds the field still and changes it in place, which on a panel is the plasma wash.

scale.line: The field's spatial frequency: low is broad blobs, high is fine detail.

NoiseMeterEffect.line: An audio VU meter rendered as a noise bar, where the volume sets how many rows light from the bottom.
NoiseMeterEffect.summary: Each row is colored by drifting Perlin noise, so a loud moment fills the full width and depth bottom-up with a drifting gradient rather than a flat bar.

fadeRate.line: How fast the trail decays each frame.

width.line: How strongly the volume drives the bar height.

PaintBrushEffect.line: Audio-reactive brush strokes: lines whose 3D endpoints oscillate on the beat over a fading field.
PaintBrushEffect.summary: Each stroke is shortened to a band-magnitude length, so the moving tip sweeps a curve. The field fades each frame, so the lines leave brush strokes rather than redrawing cleanly, and silence fades the field to black.

oscillatorOffset.line: The phase spread between the oscillating endpoints.

numLines.line: How many parallel strokes are animated.

fadeRate.line: How fast the background decays, higher for shorter strokes.

minLength.line: A stroke draws only if longer than this, so quiet bands stay off.

color_chaos.line: Random hue per line instead of a per-band gradient.

ParticlesEffect.line: A swarm of drifting particles with persistent fading trails.
ParticlesEffect.summary: Points drift, bounce off the walls and leave a fading trail behind them.

speed.line: The drift velocity.

fade.line: How long the trails persist, higher is longer tails.

PictureEffect.line: The active [Picture service](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/core/services.html#picture)'s picture on the layer, so a picture of any size shows on a layout of any size.
PictureEffect.summary: A modifier rotates, mirrors or tiles it as it does any effect, and a cube shows it on every slice.

fit.line: Keep the aspect with bands or cropped, or stretch it to the grid.
fit.more: **fit** shows the whole picture, with bands where its aspect leaves the grid empty. With **fill** it covers the grid and crops what overflows, and **stretch** distorts it to the grid's aspect.

sampling.line: One pixel per light, or the mean of the light's rectangle.
sampling.more: **point** takes the one pixel at a light's center, sharp and the fastest. With **area** each light averages its rectangle of the picture, so fine detail stays steady when a large picture shrinks onto few lights.

edgeDepth.line: How far in the edge lights look, in percent; 0 is their own share.
edgeDepth.more: A border strip's outermost lights own a sliver at the edge, where letterboxes and overscan live. Raise **edgeDepth** and they reach further in, as Hyperion's 8% does; a stride keeps the reads the same.

smoothing.line: How slowly a light eases to a new color, as a half-life; 0 is off.
smoothing.more: Raise **smoothing** and a light eases toward its new color, settling a noisy source alike on every source and board. A cut is a real jump, so **snapAbove** lands a bigger move whole; at 0 every move eases.

snapAbove.line: A channel moving further than this jumps instead of easing.

PlasmaEffect.line: Summed sine waves on orthogonal and diagonal axes make large rolling blobs, in 3D on volumetric layouts.
PlasmaEffect.summary: Four sines are summed per pixel, or five in a volume, with their average picking the palette index. A larger scale means a smaller per-pixel step, so the blobs grow bigger and calmer.

scale_x.line: Blob size along x; larger is bigger and calmer.

scale_y.line: Blob size along y, which the depth axis reuses.

PraxisEffect.line: An algorithmic palette pattern driven by two beat oscillators, a macro and a micro mutator, whose frequencies and ranges reshape the hue field over time.
PraxisEffect.summary: Each pixel's hue comes from the two mutators combined with its own position, so the pattern continually stretches, shears and rolls across the grid.

speed.line: How fast the pattern advances.

PulseEffect.line: Shells expand from a drifting origin, one per beat: a pair of fronts on a strip, a ring on a panel, a sphere in a volume.
PulseEffect.summary:
Sound fires a shell and its pitch colors it, and an idle clock keeps them arriving in a silent room.

Compare with [BeatRipples](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/effects.html#beatripples), which simulates water on a plane, where this one draws a moving front that carries it into 1D and 3D.

guide.title: At boot
guide.text: It is the effect a fresh device starts with: one beat is unmistakable, and the drifting origin shows the device running before any sound arrives.

bpm.line: Pulses a minute while nothing is heard; 0 waits for sound alone.

speed.line: How fast a shell crosses the layout, at any layout size.

thickness.line: The shell's width, as a share of the layout rather than in lights.

audioGain.line: How strongly sound fires a pulse; 0 ignores it.

drift.line: How far the origin wanders from the center; 0 pins it there.

RainbowEffect.line: A diagonal animated rainbow: the always-visible default and test effect.
RainbowEffect.summary: A pixel's hue comes from its own x plus y, walked by the clock, so the bands run diagonally.

speed.line: Animation BPM: one full hue cycle per beat.

tests.title: Control a palette preset changes only the palette
Effects teardown under a running pipeline
State one document adds an effect with its controls

RandomEffect.line: Lights one random light per frame in a random palette color over a fading background: a sparse, palette-tinted sparkle.
RandomEffect.summary: The buffer dims a little, then one light takes a random palette color, and over many frames that scatters fading sparkles across the whole volume. `fade` sets the density: less lets them linger and fill, more leaves quick specks.

fade.line: How fast prior sparkles fade to black.

RingsEffect.line: Expanding concentric rings from random centers, with additive overlap and calm defaults.
RingsEffect.summary: Each ring grows continuously and respawns somewhere fresh once it leaves the grid. Several overlap, and where two rings cross their brightness sums. [Ripples](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/effects.html#ripples) holds the sine-wave water surface, where this one is the concentric form.

count.line: How many concentric rings; a few slow ones read as clean circles.

speed.line: Expansion rate.

RipplesEffect.line: Distance from the center sets a per-column wave phase, so the lit surface ripples like water.
RipplesEffect.summary: The effect writes a height across y, so it wants real depth to read as a surface, and a flat layout collapses it to a single row. Its sibling [WaterRipple](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/effects.html#waterripple) simulates a real wave equation on a plane.

speed.line: Wave animation rate.

interval.line: Wavefront spacing; low is tight rings, high is wide.

RubiksCubeEffect.line: A 3D Rubik's Cube projected onto the volume: it scrambles, then plays its solution back one turn at a time, the six faces in their standard colors.
RubiksCubeEffect.summary: Every voxel takes the color of the nearest outer face, which is what makes a solid read as a cube. The cube is a full six-face model with the real face, row and column rotations, and `cubeSize` of 2 through 8 gives real cubes where 1 is a single block.

cubeSize.line: The cube order, its side in cells.

randomTurning.line: Turn endlessly at random instead of scramble-then-solve.

usePalette.line: Color the faces from the palette, not the classic colors.

SineEffect.line: Red, green and blue each follow a sine along one axis at a third of a turn apart: a glowing, scrolling color box.
SineEffect.summary: A flat layout holds its depth term constant, which reads as a red and green wash.

frequency.line: How many waves cross the box.

SolidEffect.line: A flat fill with five color modes: a plain RGB(W) color, the palette spread across the lights, one RMS-averaged palette color, or the palette banded along rows or columns.
SolidEffect.summary: Brightness scales every mode except Palette avg.

white.line: Its white channel, written only where the light carries one.

brightness.line: Scales the color in every mode except Palette avg.

colorMode.line: Which of the five color modes fills the layer.

minRGB.line: The band modes drop palette entries darker than this on every channel.

randomColors.line: The band modes shuffle the surviving entries, reproducibly.

SdfShapesEffect.line: A circle and a box orbit and melt into each other, drawn as signed distance fields rather than outlines.
SdfShapesEffect.summary: One distance per pixel yields three looks at once: a smooth fill, an outline, and a glow falling off into the field. The two shapes flow together like mercury rather than merely overlapping.

radius.line: Circle radius, as a fraction of the short side.

boxSize.line: Box half-extent, on the same scale.

blend.line: The melt radius, where 0 unions the shapes hard.

outline.line: Outline width, where 0 fills the shape.

glow.line: Tint the surrounding field by its distance from the shape.

AuroraEffect.line: Several noise fields, each on its own clock, read in polar coordinates and composited into curtains of light.
AuroraEffect.summary: Nothing is simulated: layers of one field at different scales interfere, and that is what reads as curtains folding through one another. `polarTable` and `polarTable16` choose the polar address table and its precision.

speed.line: Master rate, every layer scales from it; 0 freezes it.

scale.line: Noise cells across the grid; low is broad, high is fine.

layers.line: How many fields are composited, and the main cost knob.

warp.line: How far the field displaces its own sample angle.

twist.line: How much the radius shears the angle, giving the curtains their lean.

segments.line: Kaleidoscope wedges; 1 leaves the composition unfolded.

contrast.line: How much of the field lights; low is cloud, high is sharp.

octaves.line: Detail within each layer, multiplying the cost knob.

PolarNoiseEffect.line: A warped noise field addressed by angle and radius, folded into a kaleidoscope.
PolarNoiseEffect.summary: Cost scales with `octaves` and `warp`: at `warp` above 0 and `octaves` 2 it is roughly 4 noise samples per pixel. On a large wall set `octaves` to 1 or `warp` to 0, which degrades to a plain polar noise that still reads well.

guide.title: polarTable
guide.text: Each pixel's angle and radius come from a table at 2 bytes a pixel.

guide.title: polarTable16
guide.text: The table at full precision, 4 bytes a pixel.

scale.line: Noise cells across the grid; low is broad, high is fine detail.

warp.line: Domain-warp strength; 0 gives a plain field.

octaves.line: Fbm octaves, and the main cost knob.

twist.line: How much the radius shears the angle, setting the spiral.

WaterRippleEffect.line: A propagating wave simulation: drops land, their rings spread outward, reflect off the edges and interfere where they cross.
WaterRippleEffect.summary: The crossing is what a drawn ripple cannot fake, because two rings meeting have to add and cancel. Distinct from [Ripples](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/effects.html#ripples), which draws clean concentric circles; this behaves like water.

speed.line: Simulation steps a second, which is how fast the water itself moves.

dropRate.line: How often drops land, where 0 leaves the surface still.

damping.line: How fast waves lose energy, so higher is calmer water.

colorByHeight.line: Color the surface by height rather than by brightness alone.

hueBase.line: Where in the palette the still surface sits.

hueSpread.line: How far a crest and a trough reach from that.

FluidEffect.line: Light poured into a simulated medium and carried by it.
FluidEffect.summary: Every other flow here is a function of position and time. This one is state, so a jet fired now changes where everything downstream goes for seconds afterwards. On a cube every depth slice is its own medium, so the slices differ. Sized for the desktop and the P4; an S3 runs it on a small grid.

jets.line: How many places light is poured in.

force.line: How hard each jet pushes the medium.

swirl.line: How fast the jets sweep, which is what stirs vortices.

viscosity.line: How much the medium drags on itself; high is syrup, low smoke.

persistence.line: How long dye survives, as a half-life.

iterations.line: Pressure-solve effort, and the cost knob.

NebulaEffect.line: A noise field decides where light is born, a curl flow decides where it goes, and the cloud keeps folding into itself.
NebulaEffect.summary: The emitter is a field rather than a handful of dots, so light enters everywhere at once and the flow shapes a whole cloud instead of drawing trails. The cloud is held at 16 bits and dithered on the way out, which keeps a slow fade smooth.

guide.title: Cheaper fields
guide.text: `fieldScale` and `fieldRate` make the field cheaper, smaller or less often computed. That costs detail, not smoothness, since the flow still carries the cloud every frame.

speed.line: How fast the medium moves, and with it the whole cloud.

scale.line: The field's cell size: low is broad clouds, high is wisps.

contrast.line: What fraction of the field is bright enough to be born.

persistence.line: How long light survives in the flow, as a half-life.

octaves.line: Detail within the field, and its cost knob.

fieldScale.line: Compute the field at a fraction of the grid and stretch it.

fieldRate.line: Recompute the field every N frames.

TrailsEffect.line: Dots thrown into a moving medium, leaving tails the flow carries and bends.
TrailsEffect.summary: Nothing draws a tail: it is the previous frames' dots, transported along a velocity field and dimmed, which is why the flow's shape is visible in it. On a cube each depth slice gets its own flow.

speed.line: How fast the medium moves, and with it every tail.

dots.line: How many emitters are throwing light in.

scale.line: The flow field's cell size. Low gives broad sweeps, high gives eddies.

persistence.line: How long a tail survives, as a half-life.

breathe.line: How much the flow's strength rises and falls.

ColorTrailsEffect.line: Emitters pouring color into a flow that carries and folds it.
ColorTrailsEffect.summary: There is no velocity field: one noise value shifts each row sideways, one shifts each column, and the two shears compose into a swirling current. A large grid is steered by a few hundred numbers, which is why it runs where a solver does not. Compare with [Fluid](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/effects.html#fluid): the solver when the medium is the subject, this when the color is.

speed.line: How fast the emitters travel.

flow.line: How far a row or column is pushed: the shear amount.

flowSpeed.line: How fast the flow itself drifts and reverses.

scale.line: The profiles' spatial frequency: a few broad bands or many fine ones.

persistence.line: How long color survives, as a half-life.

colorSpeed.line: How fast the emitters walk the palette.

size.line: The orbit's radius and the Lissajous figure's reach.

mode.line: All three emitters, or one at a time to see what each adds.

flowType.line: The field carrying them: Noise, Radial out or Radial in.

TunnelEffect.line: A texture mapped onto the inside of an infinite tube, so the viewer appears to fly down it forever.
TunnelEffect.summary: Nothing is 3D: the angle around the center is one texture coordinate and the reciprocal of the distance is the other, which is perspective for the price of a divide.

bpm.line: How fast the tunnel flies past.

depth.line: Texture scale along the tunnel; higher is finer rings.

twist.line: Rotation per unit depth, so the tunnel corkscrews.

segments.line: Kaleidoscope the wall, where 1 leaves it plain.

octaves.line: Wall texture detail, and the cost knob.

vignette.line: Darken toward the vanishing point, so it reads as receding.

EchoEffect.line: The previous frame fed back through a zoom and rotation, dimmed, with a bright source drawn on top.
EchoEffect.summary: The trails spiral away from themselves, like a camera pointed at its own monitor. Feedback is not a primitive: once the grid can be read as a texture (`sampleWrap`), the whole family of trails, zoom blur and smear is a few lines.

zoom.line: How much the feedback grows each frame.

rotate.line: Rotation per frame, which turns the trail into a spiral.

decay.line: How fast the echo fades; higher is a shorter trail.

DissolveEffect.line: Two color fields trade places pixel by pixel in an order that looks random but is computed.
DissolveEffect.summary: The transition needs no per-pixel state and no shuffled index list, so two devices rendering the same frame dissolve identically without exchanging anything.

spread.line: How long pixels spend mid-flight; 0 gives a hard edge.

eased.line: Ease the progress instead of sweeping linearly.

scatter.line: Random order; off gives a positional wipe from the same code.

SpectrumEffect.line: An audio analyzer with real meter ballistics: bars rise fast enough to catch a transient and fall slowly enough to read.
SpectrumEffect.summary: A peak dot marks the recent maximum and drifts down. The asymmetry is the whole point: a symmetric follower either misses the hit or flickers.

attack.line: How fast a bar rises toward a new level.

release.line: How fast a bar falls back.

peakDecay.line: How fast the peak dot drifts down.

showPeaks.line: Draw the held peak above each bar.

colorByColumn.line: Color each bar by its column rather than by height.

FireworksEffect.line: Shells rise, stall, and burst into sparks that arc over and fall.
FireworksEffect.summary: Nothing schedules the apex: the shell decelerates under gravity and bursts when its vertical velocity crosses zero, so a faster launch bursts higher without a second control. The physics runs on elapsed time, so a shell and its sparks follow the same arc at any frame rate.

launchRate.line: How often a new shell goes up.

launchSpeed.line: How hard a shell is thrown, and so how high it bursts.

gravity.line: How fast everything falls, per 60 Hz of simulated time.

sparks.line: How many sparks each burst throws.

drag.line: Air resistance, which flattens the arc.

fade.line: Trail length, which is the Layer's decay rather than the pool's.

FishTankEffect.line: An aquarium on a light wall: fish of three shapes swim across a dark tank, each in its own color from the active palette, tails beating.
FishTankEffect.summary: The art carries shade roles rather than fixed colors. Each fish fills them from its own place on the palette, so one drawing yields as many colorways as there are fish. Each fish's band is a paler version of its own body color.

fish.line: How many broad tropical fish swim.

school.line: How many tiny schooling fish swim.

speed.line: Swim rate in body-lengths, the same on any grid.

spriteSize.line: Integer magnification; 0 is auto, scaling with the grid.

audioReactive.line: Each sprite follows its own band, so the scene breathes.

PacmanEffect.line: The arcade cast crossing a light wall: Pacman chomps along while the ghosts drift past, wrapping around the edges forever.
PacmanEffect.summary: The characters travel independently, each on its own path. Pacman keeps his yellow, and the ghosts take their colors from the active palette.

pacmen.line: How many Pacmen cross the wall, up to four.

ghosts.line: How many ghosts cross the wall, the arcade cast being four.

speed.line: Travel rate in sprite widths, the same on any grid.

spriteSize.line: Sprite magnification, scaled with the grid at zero.

audioReactive.line: Each sprite follows its own band, so the scene breathes.

FixedPointEffect.line: Shapes placed between pixels rather than on them.
FixedPointEffect.summary: A clock hand drawn on whole pixels jumps a pixel at a time and reads as broken. The same hand at a fractional position moves smoothly, because a pixel's brightness carries the fraction its position cannot.

demo.line: Which figure to draw, or `all` to cycle them.
demo.more: Eleven figures, from a geared clock through a spirograph to boids and a swaying tree, or `all` to cycle through them.

bpm.line: How fast the orbits and curves run; the clock keeps its own.

fade.line: How much of the previous frame survives, which leaves the trail.

dwell.line: Seconds each demo holds before `all` moves to the next.

drift.line: How far the scene wanders from center, in pixels; 0 pins it.

zoom.line: The camera pushes in and settles back; 0 holds it fixed.

MovingHeadEffect.line: Aims a rig of moving heads as one instrument, where `formation` decides how the heads relate.
MovingHeadEffect.summary: One head sweeping a sine is a demo, and a rig of them is a show. Pan and tilt sweep at different rates, so a beam traces a path rather than a line, and one control changes the rig's whole character without touching speed or range. A fixture chain is one-dimensional, so lay the rig out as a **1 x N** grid.

formation.line: How the heads move relative to each other.
formation.more: **fan** opens the beams like a hand, **mirror** sweeps two halves against each other, **chase** delays it head by head, **cross** opposes alternate heads, **unison** moves all as one.

tiltBpm.line: Tilt sweep rate in BPM, unequal to the pan rate to trace a path.

panRange.line: How much of the fixture's pan travel to use.

tiltRange.line: How much of the fixture's tilt travel to use.

panCenter.line: Where the pan sweep is centered, 128 being the middle.

tiltCenter.line: Where the tilt sweep is centered.

audioReactive.line: The beam widens with the room, each head on its own band.

gobo.line: The gobo wheel as a raw byte, see the fixture's manual.
gobo.more: Only the fixture's manual says what a value selects. `rotate` works the same way for the gobo or prism spin.

rotate.line: The gobo or prism spin as a raw byte, see the fixture's manual.

goboOnBeat.line: Roll a new gobo when the level jumps, then hold it a moment.
goboOnBeat.more: The hold stops a busy track from strobing through patterns.

FlyingToastersEffect.line: The classic screensaver on a light wall: chrome toasters with flapping wings and slices of toast drift diagonally across the dark, forever.
FlyingToastersEffect.summary: The wing flap carries a per-toaster offset, so the flock never falls into sync. The sprites carry their own colors (chrome, wing, crust), so the global palette does not apply. Needs a grid at least the toaster's size (12×9).

toast.line: How many slices of toast fly with them.

speed.line: Drift rate in sprite-widths, the same on any grid.

spriteSize.line: Integer magnification for toasters and toast; 0 is auto.

audioReactive.line: Each sprite follows its own band, so the scene breathes.

SpaceInvadersEffect.line: The 1978 formation marching down the wall: five ranks stepping sideways in the two-frame wiggle, dropping a row and reversing at each wall.
SpaceInvadersEffect.summary:
The march speeds up as the ranks thin, which is the defining mechanic.

The game plays itself in attract mode, and `player` and `fire` hand the cannon to a person. The invaders take their body color from the active palette.

guide.title: The game
guide.text: Invaders fire down and the cannon fires back. A formation that lands, or a board cleared of invaders, resets the board.

marchBpm.line: March beats per minute, two steps a beat, faster as ranks thin.

stepX.line: How far a step moves the formation sideways, in pixels.

dropY.line: How far a wall turn drops the formation, in pixels.

size.line: Magnification per art pixel: 1 on a matrix, 2 or more on a wall.

audioReactive.line: The formation steps on the beat, and silence holds it still.

player.line: The cannon, for a fader or an input; idle, the game plays it.

fire.line: Fires the cannon, one shot in the air at a time.

SpriteFountainEffect.line: A fountain that throws the project's whole sprite cast, launched from the floor on a sweeping nozzle and falling back under gravity.
SpriteFountainEffect.summary:
The cast is fish, Pacman and his ghosts, toasters and toast, and the three invaders.

Colors come from the active palette, one per sprite, held for its whole flight.

lift.line: How hard the nozzle throws, scaled with the grid.

pull.line: Gravity: gentle enough that a sprite stays legible for its whole arc.

rate.line: Sprites launched per beat of the emit clock.

emitBpm.line: Launches per minute, which sets the plume's density.

audioReactive.line: One sprite per band, so the cast maps onto the spectrum.

PongEffect.line: Two paddles rally a ball, the attract mode of the 1972 original where both players are the machine.
PongEffect.summary:
A perfect tracker would rally forever and never look like a game, so each paddle has a reaction delay and a small aiming error, re-rolled every exchange.

`player1` and `player2` are the paddles as controls, for a fader or an input, and while idle the game plays.

guide.title: Scoring
guide.text: The score shows at the top once the grid is at least 32 by 18, and the first side to 11 starts a new game.

rallyBpm.line: Ball crossings per minute, the same time on any grid.

paddle.line: Paddle length as a share of the court; short paddles miss more.

reflex.line: How sharply a paddle chases the ball; below full it lags a fast one.

spriteBall.line: Swap the square ball for a sprite, re-picked on every hit.

size.line: Integer magnification of the sprite ball, shown while it is on.

player1.line: The left paddle's height, for a fader or input; idle, the game plays.

player2.line: The right paddle's height, the same way.

BreakoutEffect.line: A paddle knocking down a wall of bricks, the attract mode of the 1976 original where the machine plays itself.
BreakoutEffect.summary: The paddle waits out a reaction delay and aims slightly off, so steep balls outrun it. The ball speeds up as bricks fall, and the paddle halves once the ball reaches the back wall. Three misses, or a cleared wall, deal a fresh one. The brick rows take their colors from the active palette.

speedBpm.line: Court crossings per minute at the serve, on any grid size.

rows.line: Rows of bricks, fewer where the grid has no room.

paddle.line: Paddle width as a percentage of the court.

reflex.line: How sharply the paddle chases; below full it lags a steep ball.

descend.line: The wall creeps down and new rows enter at the top.

audioReactive.line: Columns glow with their bands, the palette follows the volume.

player.line: The paddle, for a fader or an input; idle, the game plays it.

BallpitEffect.line: Falling balls that pile up and shove each other aside.
BallpitEffect.summary: The heap is emergent: gravity pulls, the floor stops, and contact between neighbors makes the shape. `tilt` turns the pit into a slope and the pile slides and re-settles.

balls.line: How many balls share the pit.

size.line: Contact radius in pixels: how far apart balls sit when touching.

bounce.line: How much speed a contact keeps.

tilt.line: Sideways force, turning the pit into a slope.

drag.line: Damping, so the heap settles instead of sloshing.

TruchetEffect.line: A maze of interlocking arcs that never repeats, drawn without storing a single tile.
TruchetEffect.summary: Randomly turned tiles join into continuous winding paths across the surface: the pattern looks designed, and nothing designed it. This is the representative 2D shader: no 3D, no rays, no float, and cheap on any target.

softness.line: Edge softness, which is the anti-aliasing width.

shuffle.line: Reshuffles which way the tiles face.

drift.line: Slide the pattern rather than holding it still.

VectorBallsEffect.line: A rotating 3D object drawn as shaded spheres, the demoscene classic that named the technique.
VectorBallsEffect.summary: The smallest complete demonstration of putting 3D on a panel: rotate, project, sort back to front, shade by distance, draw. Without painter's ordering a far ball paints over a near one and the object turns inside out.

size.line: A ball's radius at the object's center, in pixels.

spread.line: How far apart the balls sit.

distance.line: How far the object is from the viewer.

fade.line: Dim the far balls, which is what reads as depth.

RaymarchEffect.line: A lit 3D scene rendered by marching a ray through a distance field, one ray per pixel.
RaymarchEffect.summary: Nothing draws a sphere: the scene is a function returning the distance to the nearest surface, and the spheres emerge where each ray stops. Writing a different 3D effect means writing a different `scene()`, which is the whole API. Cost is per pixel, and `steps` trades quality against it.

guide.title: Where it runs
guide.text: It is compiled only for a chip with a hardware FPU, so a classic ESP32 does not offer it.

steps.line: Ray marching steps: the quality and cost knob.

blend.line: How much the two spheres melt into each other.

SphereMoveEffect.line: A hollow spherical shell that bounces through the 3D volume, its surface colored from the palette, leaving no trail.
SphereMoveEffect.summary: The shell sweeps the volume on a Lissajous path, breathing as it goes. Every voxel inside the one-unit shell lights from the palette, jittered so it shimmers.

speed.line: How fast the sphere moves through the volume.

SpiralEffect.line: A rotating spiral built from each pixel's angle and distance from the center.
SpiralEffect.summary: Each pixel's hue comes from its angle plus its radius times `twist`, walked by the clock. So the arms wind outward, and turning `twist` up tightens them.

twist.line: How tightly the arms wind, as hue per unit radius.

StarFieldEffect.line: A perspective starfield: stars approach the viewer from a vanishing point, brightening as they near, then respawn at depth.
StarFieldEffect.summary: Each star is a 3D point drifting toward the viewer, re-projected onto the panel every advance. A near star splays outward and flies off the edge while a distant one sits near the center. A star passing the camera respawns at the far plane.

speed.line: How fast the stars approach, where 0 pauses the field.

usePalette.line: Color the stars from the palette instead of white.

StarSkyEffect.line: Twinkling stars at random light positions, each fading in and out independently over a dark background.
StarSkyEffect.summary: A pool of stars, sized from the light count, each taking a random cell and brightness. A small per-frame chance flips a star's direction early, so the field never pulses in sync.

speed.line: Fade rate: how fast each star brightens and dims.

star_fill_ratio.line: How many stars, as a fraction of the light count.

usePalette.line: Color the stars from the active palette instead of white.

TetrixEffect.line: Falling Tetris-style blocks: each column drops a brick that lands on the growing stack, fills the column, then clears and restarts.
TetrixEffect.summary: At speed 0 each brick picks its own fall rate; otherwise all fall at the set speed. Every column runs its own state machine, so they desync into a rain of stacking bricks.

speed.line: Fall speed, where 0 gives each brick a random speed.

oneColor.line: One advancing palette color for every brick, not one each.

TextEffect.line: Renders a multi-line string in a bitmap font, static by default or as a wrapping marquee.
TextEffect.summary: Static text is laid out top-left, each newline dropping one font height, and clipped where it runs off the grid. Turn on `scroll` to march the whole block leftward as a marquee. Text color comes from the active palette.

text.line: The string to show; each line renders on its own row.

scroll.line: Off is static, on a horizontal marquee.

speed.line: Marquee speed, used when `scroll` is on.

hue.line: Palette index for the text color.

WaveEffect.line: An oscilloscope waveform scrolls across the grid with a fading trail.
WaveEffect.summary: Six selectable shapes: sawtooth, triangle, sine, square, sin3 and noise. Each column plots one point of a moving wave, so the lit points trace a scrolling curve.

bpm.line: Travel speed, as phase advance per minute.

fade.line: How much trail each frame keeps; 0 clears it at once.

BlockModifier.line: Expands a 1D effect into concentric square rings: its position along the strip becomes the ring, so a gradient draws nested squares.
BlockModifier.summary: The square sibling of [Circle](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/modifiers.html#circle), which draws round rings.

CheckerboardModifier.line: Masks the layer in a checkerboard: the lights on the "off" squares stay dark, the rest show the effect unchanged.

size.line: The edge of a checker square, in lights.

invert.line: Swap which squares show the effect and which stay dark.

MoonLiveModifier.line: The coordinate transform written as text on the running device: mirror the pattern, shift it, swap its axes.
MoonLiveModifier.summary: A compiled modifier is a class and a reflash, where a script is a line of text applied as you type, and every control it declares appears on the card. The language is [MoonLive](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/moonlive.html).

guide.title: One coordinate at a time
guide.text:
A script transforms one coordinate and needs no loop, because the Layer already calls it once per physical light while it builds the mapping.

`setXYZ(x, y, z)` writes the transformed position, as `setRGB(index, r, g, b)` writes a color: a mirror is `void modifyLogical() { setXYZ(width - 1 - xPos, yPos, zPos); }`.

guide.title: Read the grid rather than assuming it
guide.text: A mirror written against a fixed 255 sends every light of a 16-wide grid outside it, and the Layer drops each one: the fixture goes black with no error. Read `width` instead. A computed coordinate arrives at full width, so `767 - xPos` is 767 on a 768-wide wall.

guide.title: What a script can transform
guide.text: A script drives the per-light hook, so a transform keeping the box its size works; one halving it, as the built-in Mirror does, needs the compiled modifier. A script that fails to compile shows the parse error, and coordinates pass through.

script.line: Which `.mlm` script runs, picked from the library and edited here.

CircleModifier.line: Expands a 1D effect into concentric circular rings: its position along the strip becomes the radius, so a gradient draws nested circles.
CircleModifier.summary: The round sibling of [Block](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/modifiers.html#block), which draws square rings.

MirrorModifier.line: Folds the far half of the box back onto the near half, mirroring the image across its center on each axis you choose.
MirrorModifier.summary: In 2D one quadrant shows in all four, in 3D one octant in all eight.

mirrorX.line: Mirror across the center along x.

mirrorY.line: Mirror across the center along y.

mirrorZ.line: Mirror across the center along z.

MultiplyModifier.line: Tiles the image across the box, a number of times per axis, and can mirror every other tile into a kaleidoscope.
MultiplyModifier.summary: Two tiles with mirroring on is a plain mirror.

multiplyX.line: Tiles along x, one meaning none.

multiplyY.line: Tiles along y, one meaning none.

multiplyZ.line: Tiles along z, one meaning none.

mirrorX.line: Reflect every other tile along x.

mirrorY.line: Reflect every other tile along y.

mirrorZ.line: Reflect every other tile along z.

PinwheelModifier.line: Remaps the grid into petals around the center, so a line or a 2D effect turns into a rotating flower or spokes.
PinwheelModifier.summary: The angle to each light picks its petal, and the radius runs along it; swirl, symmetry and z-twist bend the pattern.

petals.line: How many petals radiate from the center.

swirl.line: How far a petal bends into a spiral, negative bending the other way.

symmetry.line: How many times the pattern repeats around the turn.

zTwist.line: How far the petals twist from one z layer to the next.

RandomMapModifier.line: Moves every light to another, each one exactly once, and reshuffles on a beat: the arrangement scrambles while the content stays.

bpm.line: Reshuffles per minute, zero freezing the arrangement.

RegionModifier.line: Crops the layer to a rectangle given in percentages of each axis, so it holds when the layout is resized; outside it is dark.
RegionModifier.summary: Beyond 0 and 100 the window slides partly or wholly out of view.

startX.line: Where the region starts along x, in percent of the axis.

startY.line: Where it starts along y, in percent.

startZ.line: Where it starts along z, in percent.

endX.line: Where the region ends along x, in percent of the axis.

endY.line: Where it ends along y, in percent.

endZ.line: Where it ends along z, in percent.

RippleXZModifier.line: Collapses an axis to a single plane, so an effect drawn along the other axes ripples across the whole box.

shrink.line: Collapse the chosen axes to a single plane.

towardsX.line: Collapse x, so each column shares one light.

towardsZ.line: Collapse z, so each x-y plane is shared across depth.

RotateModifier.line: Turns the 2D image around its center, continuously, at the speed you set.

speed.line: How fast the image turns.

TransposeModifier.line: Swaps a pair of axes and can flip each one, so the image rotates or mirrors without the effect redrawing.

XY.line: Swap x and y, rows becoming columns.

inverse X.line: Flip x after the swaps, so it reads back to front.

HueDriver.line: Drives Philips Hue bulbs as pixels: each color bulb in the driver's window becomes one pixel, pushed to the bridge over its HTTP API.
HueDriver.summary: The same shape as [NetworkSend](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html#networksend), over HTTP rather than UDP. One command goes to the bridge every half second, so it gives smooth ambient color, not strobing. Up to 32 bulbs, a LAN's worth, which bounds the driver's memory.

bridgeIp.line: The bridge's LAN IP, entered in the UI (4 octets).

appKey.line: The Hue app key, filled by `pair`; a password, so masked and kept out of documents.

pair.line: Press it, then the bridge's link button within about 30 s to claim a key.

room.line: All rooms, or the one whose lights are driven.

light.line: Narrows the driven lights to one light of that room; 0 is All.

start.line: The first light of the shared buffer this driver reads.

count.line: How many lights it reads from `start`; blank reads them all.
count.more: So drivers share one buffer: a status LED takes `start 0, count 1` and the strip `start 1`.

NetworkSendDriver.line: Streams the buffer over UDP as Art-Net, E1.31 or DDP, its packets paced so receivers keep up, to Falcon and Advatek controllers, xLights and LedFx.
NetworkSendDriver.summary: One driver feeds many receivers, each taking a contiguous run of the window under its own address. A wall of tubes is one driver, the twin of one LED driver fanning out to several lanes.

guide.title: Mixed fixtures
guide.text:
A chain of mixed fixtures needs one driver per fixture type, each with its own `start`, `count` and `fixture`, the richest motion fixture first.

| driver | window | fixtures |
|---|---|---|
| A | `start 0`, `count 2` | the two big pan/tilt/zoom heads |
| B | `start 2`, `count 4` | four smaller pan/tilt heads |
| C | `start 6`, `count 10` | ten RGBW pars |

localBrightness.line: This driver's dim, multiplied with the global brightness.

curve.line: How brightness maps to output: CIE 1931, a gamma, or linear.

fixture.line: The fixture profile applied per light, for channel order and white.
fixture.more: A reorder or a reboot keeps it. After renaming the profile, re-pick it: the next reboot falls back to the default.

whiteMode.line: How the white channel is derived, shown when the profile carries one.

fixtureRef.line: The profile name an older config saved, read once and then emptied.

protocol.line: The wire protocol: Art-Net, E1.31 or DDP; the port follows.

addressing.line: How packets travel: unicast, Art-Net broadcast or E1.31 multicast.
addressing.more: Art-Net 4 requires unicast; broadcast loads every host. E1.31 `multicast` needs [IGMP snooping](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/explanation/architecture/moonlight.html#multicast-and-igmp-snooping), and the status says when it is dropped.

hosts.line: Receiver addresses or names, in fan-out order; blank idles.
hosts.more: A name resolves in the background, `.local` by mDNS and anything else by DNS. It sends nothing until it first resolves, keeps its last address while it stops answering, and the status names the ones still waiting.

lightsPerHost.line: Lights per receiver; blank splits evenly, one number to all, a list each.

universe_start.line: The first universe, emitted verbatim with no one-based adjust; DDP ignores it.

start.line: The first light of the shared buffer this driver reads.

count.line: How many lights it reads from `start`; blank reads them all.
count.more: So drivers share one buffer: a status LED takes `start 0, count 1` and the strip `start 1`.

fps.line: Frame-rate limit, so a fast render tick does not flood the LAN.

packet_gap.line: Microseconds between a frame's packets; 0 sends a burst.
packet_gap.more: The pause lets a receiver keep up, sent from a task so the render loop never waits.

PreviewDriver.line: Streams a true-shape 3D preview of the layer to the web UI.
PreviewDriver.summary:
Only the real lights are sent, at their real positions, so a sphere, ring or arbitrary map shows in its true shape. It is the one boot-wired driver.

It streams on its own WebSocket channel so a large frame never delays the control plane. It sends only while a viewer is watching, and moving heads show their beam.

guide.title: Close it when you do not need it
guide.text: The device renders preview frames only while the preview pane is open. Dismissing the pane stops that work entirely, which frees the device and keeps the UI responsive on a large layout. Worth doing while you edit effects on a big wall.

guide.title: It thins itself out
guide.text: When the connection cannot carry full detail, the preview shows a regular sample of the lights and the status reads `2 watching · 1/4`. Drop-free stretches earn detail back a step at a time. A slow effect drops nothing, so it never costs detail.

guide.title: If the preview looks choppy
guide.text: The connection is the cause, not the device: frames are dropped rather than queued, so the wall itself is never held up. Lower `targetFps` to keep full detail at a slower rate.

targetFps.line: The rate the preview aims for: lower for detail, raise for smoothness.

tests.title: Effects teardown under a running pipeline

NdiDriver.line: Publishes the layer as an NDI video source that OBS, Resolume, TouchDesigner or any NDI receiver finds by name on the network.
NdiDriver.summary:
The grid becomes the frame, one light per pixel, output correction applied, so a receiver sees what the wall sees. Where [Preview](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html#preview) draws the lights for a person, this hands the same frame to a production tool.

Desktop only, as no NDI runtime exists for the ESP32 chips. A board reaches the same tools over Art-Net, sACN or DDP with [NetworkSend](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html#networksend), and takes them in with [NetworkReceive](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/effects.html#networkreceive).

guide.title: The NDI runtime
guide.text: You install it yourself; without it the driver says so and nothing else changes. The steps: [installing the NDI runtime](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/watching-the-output.html#installing-the-ndi-runtime).

guide.title: Receivers
guide.text: To see the output you need a receiver. NDI Video Monitor, part of NDI Tools, is the simplest; OBS gains an NDI Source through the DistroAV plugin. MoonLight appears under the name in `sourceName`, or the device's own name when that is blank.

guide.title: Status line
guide.text:
| It says | It means |
|---|---|
| `NDI runtime not installed` | Install it: [Watch the output as video](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonwalk.html#watch-output) |
| `could not create the NDI source` | The runtime is there but refused, usually a name clash with another source |
| `sending <w>x<h> at <n> fps` | Live; look for it in your receiver |

curve.line: How brightness maps to output: CIE 1931, a gamma, or linear.

fixture.line: The fixture profile applied per light, for channel order and white.
fixture.more: A reorder or a reboot keeps it. After renaming the profile, re-pick it: the next reboot falls back to the default.

whiteMode.line: How the white channel is derived, shown when the profile carries one.

fixtureRef.line: The profile name an older config saved, read once and then emptied.

sourceName.line: The name a receiver lists; blank uses the device's own.

fps.line: Frame-rate ceiling, declared in every frame.

HlsDriver.line: Streams the layer as H.264 over HLS from the device's own HTTP server, which a TV, VLC or a browser can play.
HlsDriver.summary:
Open the `url` the card shows in VLC, a browser or an Apple TV. Where [Ndi](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html#ndi) feeds production tools, this feeds anything that plays video.

The grid becomes the frame, output correction applied. Latency is HLS's own, 2 to 5 seconds, so this is for watching rather than live-control feedback. The card's status line carries the state, the drops, or why the encoder stopped.

guide.title: ffmpeg
guide.text: It runs on the desktop, where you install ffmpeg yourself and then open the stream ([Watching the output](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/watching-the-output.html#installing-ffmpeg)).

guide.title: On the ESP32-P4
guide.text: There is no ffmpeg: the chip's H.264 block encodes. It takes even dimensions from 80x80 to 1920x2032; an odd wall has its scale doubled, a larger wall is refused.

fixture.more: A reorder or a reboot keeps it. After renaming the profile, re-pick it: the next reboot falls back to the default.

fixtureRef.line: The profile name an older config saved, read once and then emptied.

targetFps.line: Encode-rate ceiling, and the bandwidth knob: bitrate follows.
targetFps.more: The bitrate follows from grid size and rate, near 800 kbit for 512x512 at 30 fps. Lower the rate to save bandwidth: fewer frames beat a blockier picture.

scale.line: Video pixels per light, 0 being auto; one factor for both axes.
scale.more: Auto lifts both axes to 80, the encoder's minimum, so a 20x10 wall streams as 160x80. Raising it on a large wall buys nothing a player's zoom does not.

encoder.line: Which ffmpeg encoder to use; hardware ones offload the encode.
encoder.more: `libx264` is software, the default. Hardware encoders suit large grids: `h264_videotoolbox` on a Mac, `h264_v4l2m2m` on a Raspberry Pi, `h264_nvenc` on NVIDIA. One your ffmpeg lacks reads `encoder exited - check ffmpeg`.

url.line: The address to open in VLC or a browser, relative to this device.

RtspDriver.line: Serves the layer as an H.264 stream a player pulls over RTSP, with a fraction of the delay HLS carries.
RtspDriver.summary:
HLS ships whole segments and a player buffers several before it starts, so a viewer sees seconds ago. RTSP sends each frame as the encoder produces it, which makes this the remote view to reach for.

Point VLC or ffplay at the `url` the card shows. It runs on the ESP32-P4 and the desktop, and shares one encoder with [Hls](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html#hls), so only one of the two runs at a time.

guide.title: Playing it
guide.text: Open the `url` in VLC or ffplay ([Watching the output](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/watching-the-output.html#playing-an-rtsp-stream)). The second of RTSP and HLS to start reports that the encoder is in use.

guide.title: One viewer at a time
guide.text: A new connection takes the session over, and the displaced viewer sees its connection close. A network that blocks the UDP port the viewer names leaves the stream silent ([Watching the output](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/watching-the-output.html#when-an-rtsp-stream-stays-silent)).

guide.title: The delay that remains
guide.text: H.264 emits a frame once it has the whole frame, and a decoder holds one more, so tens of milliseconds stay. RTSP removes HLS's segment buffering, the seconds.

curve.line: How brightness maps to output: CIE 1931, a gamma, or linear.

fixture.line: The fixture profile applied per light, for channel order and white.
fixture.more: A reorder or a reboot keeps it. After renaming the profile, re-pick it: the next reboot falls back to the default.

whiteMode.line: How the white channel is derived, shown when the profile carries one.

fixtureRef.line: The profile name an older config saved, read once and then emptied.

targetFps.more: The rate is a ceiling: a heavy effect that renders at 8 fps streams at 8 fps. Each module's tick time in the UI says which effect spends it.

url.line: The address to play in VLC or ffplay, with the device's own IP.

PanelCardDriver.line: Streams the buffer to ColorLight 5A-75 receiving cards as raw Ethernet, taking the place of the sending card that normally feeds them.
PanelCardDriver.summary: The board renders and sends, so it replaces a host PC driving the same wall. There are no geometry controls: the wall comes from the [Layout](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/layouts.html), cut into card rows.

guide.title: Why 1 Gbit
guide.text: The cards need 1000 Mbps for wire time, not bandwidth: they latch on the sync frame, so a whole frame must arrive inside the inter-frame window. At 100 Mbit expect tearing or wrong rows; the driver warns but still sends ([Panel cards](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/hardware/panel-cards.html#the-one-hardware-fact-that-decides-everything)).
