fixture.more: A reorder or a reboot keeps it. After renaming the profile, re-pick it: the next reboot falls back to the default.

whiteMode.line: How the white channel is derived, shown when the profile carries one.

fixtureRef.line: The profile name an older config saved, read once and then emptied.

firmware.line: The card firmware; a wrong one and the wall barely updates.
firmware.more: v13 and newer acts on the second copy of brightness and sync, which go out twice; v12 and older on the first ([Panel cards](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/hardware/panel-cards.html#7-card-firmware-and-the-flicker)).

interface.line: The network adapter the frames go out on.
interface.more: `none (capture only)` records frames without sending. Sending needs root or `CAP_NET_RAW` on Linux, BPF on macOS, Npcap on Windows ([steps](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/hardware/panel-cards.html#6-from-a-desktop)).

start.line: The first light of the shared buffer this driver reads.

count.line: How many lights it reads from `start`; blank reads them all.
count.more: So drivers share one buffer: a status LED takes `start 0, count 1` and the strip `start 1`.

fps.line: Frame-rate limit, so a fast render tick does not saturate the link.

Hub75Driver.line: Drives HUB75 LED panels straight from the board's own pins, with no receiving card in between.
Hub75Driver.summary: The sibling of [PanelCard](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html#panelcard), which drives the same panels over Ethernet. A [MoonHub75](https://moonmodules.org/projects/hardware/#moonhub75-pcb) runs a 64x64 1/32-scan panel at 6-bit and 1,508 Hz; larger walls wait on reports.

guide.title: Which of the two paths
guide.text: A receiving card ([PanelCard](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html#panelcard)) earns its place above roughly 16,384 pixels; below that this driver is the small end of the split. [HUB75 panels](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/hardware/hub75-panels.html#which-of-the-two-paths) has the choice.

localBrightness.line: This driver's dim, multiplied with the global brightness.

curve.line: How brightness maps to output: CIE 1931, a gamma, or linear.

fixture.line: The fixture profile applied per light, for channel order and white.
fixture.more: A reorder or a reboot keeps it. After renaming the profile, re-pick it: the next reboot falls back to the default.

whiteMode.line: How the white channel is derived, shown when the profile carries one.

fixtureRef.line: The profile name an older config saved, read once and then emptied.

board.line: The board's wiring: picking one fills the fourteen pins, Custom keeps yours.
board.more: A published map hides the pin rows, which stay bound. A pin on flash or PSRAM is refused. Boards and the R1/G1/B1 naming trap: [HUB75 panels](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/hardware/hub75-panels.html#which-board).

peripheral.line: The silicon block that drives the panel, LCD_CAM or Parlio, where the chip has both.
peripheral.more: A P4 has one LCD_CAM and one Parlio, so a board already driving WS2812 strips from one needs the panel on the other. Only you know which way round.

scanRate.line: The panel's scan rate: 1/8, 1/16 or 1/32, read off the panel.
scanRate.more: Two panels of identical dimensions can scan differently, so the size does not give the rate. A 1/32-scan panel needs `e`; on 1/16 panels that pin is free.

bitDepth.line: Bit planes per frame: color levels against refresh and memory.
bitDepth.more: Depth costs refresh and memory linearly. Brightness shortens each plane's lit time, so full white lights about a third of the time at 6-bit.

clockEdge.line: The edge the chips sample on; every pixel one column over means the other.

refresh.line: The measured refresh rate: the number to report when a panel flickers.

RmtLedDriver.line: Addressable WS2812B-class LEDs on a handful of strands, clocked by the chip's RMT peripheral.
RmtLedDriver.summary: The classic choice, and the one that needs no DMA peripheral: for more than a few strands see [ParallelLed](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html#parallelled). Flicker on LEDs that should be off is signal integrity rather than firmware, and [the signal integrity playbook](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/troubleshooting.html#stray-pixels-or-wrong-colors-on-lights-that-should-be-off) walks the checks.

pins.line: Data GPIO list: `18,17,16` or ranges like `20-23`. Empty idles.

timing.line: Wire bit rate: a 12V WS2811 needs 400kHz, most LEDs the faster.

t0hNs.line: Custom timing: how long a 0 bit stays high, in nanoseconds.

t1hNs.line: Custom timing: how long a 1 bit stays high, in nanoseconds.

periodNs.line: Custom timing: the whole bit cell, in nanoseconds.

loopbackTest.line: TX to RX self-test: send a known pattern, verify the capture.

loopbackTxPin.line: TX pin override for the test; unset uses the first data pin.

loopbackRxPin.line: Jumper this to the TX pin: the test reads the pattern back here.

loopbackFrame.line: Send whole frames back to back and verify every bit.

PwmLightDriver.line: Lights whose channels are each a pin, pulsed by the chip's PWM: a bulb, an analog RGB, RGBW or RGBCCT strip, a QuinLED An-Penta controller, on any ESP32's LEDC.
PwmLightDriver.summary: The fixture profile names what each pin carries, so the light count is the pins divided by the profile's channels. One timer serves the driver and each pin takes one channel, up to 16 on the classic ESP32 and 6 on the C3. The channels' pulses start spread over the period, so full white never switches all at once.

pins.line: One GPIO per output channel, in the fixture's channel order.

bits.line: PWM resolution, which sets the pulse rate.
bits.more: Each bit more halves the pulse rate: 12 bits pulse at 19531 Hz, QuinLED's recommendation, and 16 at 1220 Hz. More bits fade smoother, fewer band less on camera. The C3 and S3 reach 14.

frequency.line: The pulse rate the resolution gives, to read against a fixture's datasheet.

ParallelLedDriver.line: WS2812B-class LEDs on up to 16 strands clocked out at once by a DMA peripheral, which makes a large wall possible.
ParallelLedDriver.summary: Each strand takes the next run of lights on its own GPIO. Switching between peripherals is a control change, with no reflash. For a few strands see [RmtLed](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html#rmtled), and for a Teensy 4.1 its [hardware page](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/hardware/teensy-4-1.html).

guide.title: Which peripheral
guide.text: Start with `i80`. Choose `MoonI80` for frames too big for memory or a pin expander, `Parlio` on a P4, `GPIO-DMA` on a Teensy 4.1. [LED drivers](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/hardware/led-drivers.html#which-one) has the chips, limits and wiring.

frameTime.line: What one frame costs on the wire: the pipeline's headroom.

peripheral.line: The DMA peripheral that clocks the strands out, filtered to what the chip supports.

doubleBuffer.line: Encode the next frame while this one clocks out, where supported.
doubleBuffer.more: Leave it on: a tick costs the longer of encode and wire, not their sum, for one extra DMA buffer and 8 to 20 ms of latency. A board without room falls back to one buffer.

clockPin.line: The i80 write strobe (WR): the pixel clock, and the expander's shift clock.

dcPin.line: The i80 bus's data/command select, which `LCD-IDF` mandates though WS2812 ignores it.

pinExpander.line: A 74HCT595 per data pin: each pin then drives 8 strands.
pinExpander.more: It buys pins, not memory: the frame grows eightfold, about 1.1 KB per light, up to 64 strands. `i80` stops at about 96 lights per strand, `MoonI80` drives 128.

latchPin.line: The 74HCT595 latch (RCLK) pin, needed with the expander.

shiftOverclock.line: Shift the '595 at 26.67 MHz, not 20, for short wires; off if a panel scrambles.

useRing.line: Stream the frame as a ring of small internal buffers, or send it whole from one block.

ringSnapshot.line: Copy each frame before the ring sends it, so a frame never mixes with the next.

ringAuto.line: Size the ring by itself and show the numbers it picked in the controls below.

ringRows.line: Lights per DMA buffer: the ring's grain, and the RAM against interrupt-rate lever.

ringBufs.line: How many buffers the DMA circulates, each `ringRows` rows of internal RAM.

ringPadUs.line: Inter-buffer zero-pad in µs, buying refill deadline at a linear frame-time cost.

ringDbg.line: The ring's live counters, once a second; `ab` counts lost frames, 0 on a healthy ring.

loopbackTest.line: TX to RX self-test: send a known pattern, bit-verify the capture.

loopbackTxPin.line: TX pin override for the test; unset uses lane 0.

loopbackRxPin.line: Jumper this to the TX pin: the self-test reads the pattern back here.

loopbackStrand.line: Strand carrying the test pattern, expander mode only.
loopbackStrand.more: Strand 0 is Q7, strand S is Q(7 - S%8): jumper it to `loopbackRxPin`. The '595 is 5 V: divide it ([LED drivers](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/hardware/led-drivers.html#testing-the-wire-with-the-loopback)).

loopbackIntrusive.line: ON rides the live pipeline, OFF rebuilds a private bus.

HttpServerModule.line: The embedded HTTP server and WebSocket: it serves the web UI and the REST API behind it.
HttpServerModule.summary: The routes are in The REST API, and the layering in What it is allowed to include.

port.line: The port the server listens on.
port.more: 8080 on the desktop and 80 on a device. A change applies when the server next opens: why.

SystemModule.line: The device's identity and vitals: its name, how long it has run, and the memory and tick it renders at.
SystemModule.summary: The name is the one the network sees, behind mDNS `<name>.local`, the access point SSID and the DHCP hostname. The readings are described under What it reports in the header.

guide.title: Safe mode
guide.text: Two failed boots in a row start the next boot with the LEDs off, no MoonLive script and at most 1,024 lights. A failed boot is a crash, a brownout, or a power loss within a minute of starting. Every boot raises the lights over five seconds.

deviceName.line: The name behind mDNS, the access point and DHCP.
deviceName.more: Anything but letters, digits and hyphens is coerced to a valid hostname, and a rename reaches the network within a tick.

deviceModel.line: The board model, which selects the installer's catalog entry.
deviceModel.more: Tooling sets it, since a device cannot identify its own hardware.

firmware.line: The build variant, kept for the MoonBase recovery image to read.

maxBlock.line: The largest free internal block, which bounds one allocation.

missing scripts.line: Shipped scripts a module names and the device lacks; an open page downloads them.

flashMode.line: How the chip reads its flash, such as QIO or DIO.

mac.line: The hardware address, which tooling identifies the device by.

sdk.line: The SDK version the firmware is built on.

mode.line: How much of the UI is shown, cumulative.
mode.more: User shows the essentials, expert adds the 🎚️ controls, developer the 🔧 ones. Only the UI reads it.

factory reset.line: Delete every setting and preset and restart as freshly installed.
factory reset.more: Press twice to confirm. Scripts and other files stay.

logLevel.more: Warn by default. The first 60 seconds always log at Info, which is when the installer reads the IP.

wifiCoproc.line: The firmware version of the separate WiFi chip.

ControlModule.line: A control desk of switches, encoders, faders and preset pads that puts the device into a named state.
ControlModule.summary: Eight switches, encoders and faders sit above 64 preset pads, laid out like a Mackie-style desk (X-Touch, QCon Pro G2), so a physical surface maps onto it.

guide.title: The surface
guide.text:
Each switch, encoder and fader drives any control you assign; right-click an encoder to see its binding. The first switch drives the master on/off and the first fader the global brightness.

From the second slot on, an unassigned slot follows the effect enabled last.

guide.title: Presets
guide.text: Click a pad to apply its preset, drag to rearrange. A pad is tinted by its role: layout blue, effects violet, driver green, service amber. [Presets](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/presets.html) has the rest.

guide.title: Home Assistant
guide.text: Only effects presets reach Home Assistant, so a hub never rewires pins or geometry. [Home automation](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/home-automation.html#presets-in-home-assistant) has the setup.

display.line: The strip above the desk: what the surface last touched, in words.
display.more: Five seconds after a touch it shows MoonLight, and five more the device's name.

presets.line: One pad per preset file. Click applies, right-click names, drag rearranges.
presets.more: Right-click a pad to rename it, delete it or save over it. A pad is a position: slot 14 stays slot 14.

name.line: The name the next save gives its preset.
name.more: Printable characters, up to 31, without slash, backslash or dot: it becomes the file name.

slot.line: The pad the next save lands on.
slot.more: Unset, a save takes the pad its preset already holds, else the first free pad.

source.line: The module the next save writes, by name.
source.more: A container from the pad editor, or any card from its own save button.

save.line: Saves the source module as the named preset.

Services.line: The container for the user-added Service modules, the capability bridges a device provides or consumes.
Services.summary: A service is added and removed at runtime, the core twin of the light domain's Effects and Drivers. Fixed device infrastructure, such as identity and network, lives under System.

AudioService.line: The audio source the audio-reactive effects read: a level, sixteen bands and the peak.
AudioService.summary: Local analyzes a microphone, line-in or capture device here. Receive network follows a peer's WLED-compatible audio, and Simulate synthesizes a song for demos. A local source can send its analysis on to other devices.

guide.title: Choosing a source
guide.text: Simulate needs nothing. Receive network needs a WLED-compatible sender. Local idles on an ESP32 until real GPIOs are entered, and captures the picked device at once on desktop.

guide.title: Wiring and capture
guide.text: Microphone wiring, setting the levels and capturing what a machine plays are in [Audio input](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/audio-input.html).

mode.line: The source: a synthesized signal, the network, or its own input.

micMode.line: Which kind of microphone is wired, I2S or two-wire PDM.
micMode.more: PDM uses `wsPin` as its clock and `sdPin` as its data, as the QuinLED Dig-Next-2's onboard mic does.

sckPin.line: The bit clock GPIO, unset until entered.

wsPin.line: The word select GPIO, or the clock of a PDM mic.

sdPin.line: The data GPIO, unset until entered.

mclkPin.line: The master clock an ADC or codec needs, unset for a plain mic.

codec.line: The codec in front of the microphone, `none` for a part that speaks I2S itself.

codecAddr.line: The codec's 7-bit address on the board's I2C bus.
codecAddr.more: 0x18 for an ES8311, 0x40 to 0x43 for an ES7210 by its strapping. The bus is [I2cBus](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/core/system.html#i2c-bus).

device.line: The capture input, `default` following the system setting.

sampleRate.line: The mic or ADC sample rate.

levels.line: Who sets the display window: the two sliders, or the learner.
levels.more: Automatic maps each band's own range onto the window, so treble reads level with bass.

floor.line: The silence threshold: below it a band reads as nothing.
floor.more: Raise it until a quiet room reads still, or the learner maps the room's noise onto the whole display.

gain.line: The window's width, a higher value running the display hotter.
gain.more: The default suits a quiet MEMS mic, so turn it down hard for a loopback device or everything clips.

send audio.line: Send the local analysis as audio-sync packets.

addressing.line: How the analysis travels: multicast, which WLED hears, or unicast.
addressing.more: Unicast to `hosts` reaches a few MoonLight boards faster on WiFi, which retries it.

hosts.line: The boards a unicast send reaches, addresses or names.

simulate.line: The pattern: a plausible song, or a test march.

syncPort.line: The UDP port both directions use, matching on both ends.
syncPort.more: WLED listens on 11988, so another port is not WLED-compatible.

level RMS.line: The level of the audio driving the effects, from any source.

onsets.line: The beats heard per second and their spectral flux.

peakHz.line: The dominant frequency of the audio driving the effects.

PictureService.line: The picture the Picture effect samples onto the lights, from one source at a time.
PictureService.summary: One picture service is active at a time, as with Audio, and any number of effects read its picture.

source.more: The test pattern is a test card in the layout of Philips' PM5544, drawn at any size. With **usb capture**, MJPEG from an HDMI grabber fills the picture at its set size.

fps.line: Frames a second asked of a capture device, which streams the nearest rate it offers.

width.line: The picture's width in pixels, and the most a capture scales its frames to.

height.line: The picture's height in pixels, under the same ceiling as the width.

OscService.line: Receives OSC over the network and writes it onto this device's controls, so a fader in Resolume, TouchDesigner or TouchOSC drives MoonLight.
OscService.summary: A surface addresses the surface: the faders, encoders and switches the control module owns, which decides what each one drives. Everything lands in the same control writes the API and the UI use, so every validator still runs.

guide.title: Getting a surface working
guide.text:
Turn on listening, and on feedback so the faders follow the device. A phone or tablet needs a free app and one session file.

[Control a device over OSC](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonwalk.html#osc-control) has the steps.

guide.title: The addresses
guide.text: The addresses are a public contract, so a layout built on them keeps working. Send `/mm/hello` and the device sends every value again. [Control surfaces](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/control-surface.html#the-osc-addresses) lists them.

listen.line: Receive OSC, which writes controls with no password.
listen.more: Off, the device ignores every surface. Turn it on only on a network you trust (why).

port.line: The UDP port to listen on, the one TouchOSC uses out of the box.

feedback.line: Mirror every change back to the surface, making this a surface, not a remote: feedback.
feedback.more: Off by default, since it sends traffic nobody asked for. It keeps a client honest and moves a motorized fader.

addressing.line: Where feedback goes: `unicast` to the hosts, or `multicast` to the group.

hosts.line: Addresses or names feedback goes to (unicast).
hosts.more: Empty answers whoever wrote last, which finds a surface on its own. Fill it to send feedback somewhere else.

group.line: The multicast group feedback goes to and this device joins.
group.more: Every listening device with the same group joins it. The default sits beside discovery's own group, so a second rig on the same network picks another.

feedbackPort.line: The UDP port the client listens on for feedback.
feedbackPort.more: Differs from the port this device listens on; Open Stage Control calls it `osc-port`.

I2cBusModule.line: The board's I2C bus: its two pins, opened once and shared by every device on it, with a scan that detects them.
I2cBusModule.summary: A device on the bus, such as the [Audio](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/core/services.html#audio) codec, names only its own address; the wires are stated here, once per board. The pins default to unused, so a board without an I2C device claims no GPIO.

guide.title: Reading the scan
guide.text: The scan names each answering address by the module driving it, as `0x18 Audio (ES8311)`. A claimed address that stays silent reads `no answer`: check the wiring and the device's power.

sda.line: The bus data pin; a board's catalog entry sets it.

scl.line: The bus clock pin; a board's catalog entry sets it.

result.line: Each address found, named by the module driving it, cut off cleanly past about three.

TasksModule.line: A read-only diagnostic showing what runs where: the tasks, and the modules inside each.
TasksModule.summary: You cannot optimize which module runs on which core until you can see it. Each task has its modules nested beneath it. The list is empty on the desktop.

guide.title: Reading a task row
guide.text:
A row shows the task's name, state, core, priority and the minimum free stack seen. Expand it for its modules, each as `Name · Nus · NB · Nheap`, and a closing `∑ modules` line that cross-checks them against the tick.

A `cpu` percentage appears only in a profiling build, since the run-time counter costs about 5% of the tick.

core0.line: What executes on the first core.

core1.line: What executes on the second core, empty on a single-core chip.

PinsModule.line: A read-only map of which module owns each GPIO, for what role, and whether the pin is safe for it.
PinsModule.summary: It is keyed by physical GPIO, the way an OS device manager or a board template is. It walks the live tree for every claimed pin, holds no state, and flags double claims.

guide.title: Reading the map
guide.text:
A row shows the GPIO, its owner and role, and the live direction, level and drive.

A row takes a colored edge when unsafe: red for a reserved or double-claimed pin, yellow for a driven role on a strap.

The [GPIO usage reference](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/hardware/gpio-usage.html) lists the pins per chip.

ButtonService.line: A list of push buttons, each on its own GPIO, each driving a control.
ButtonService.summary: A press and a UI click are the same thing to whatever they drive. A foot pedal needs no module of its own, being electrically a momentary switch.

guide.title: What a row does
guide.text: Each row binds one pin to a target, a surface control such as `Control.switch1`. Its kind toggles the target, sets a value while held and 0 on release, or nudges the target by a value. A catalog board's first button targets `Control.switch1`, which switches the lights and their relay.

guide.title: Wiring
guide.text: A switch to ground with the internal pull-up is active low, the usual wiring. A switch feeding 3V3 is active high. The live pressed readout shows a button working before it is bound.

debounceMs.line: How long a level must hold before it counts as a press, shared by every button.

buttons.line: The buttons, each with a pin, its wiring, a live pressed readout and a target.

GamepadService.line: A gamepad's buttons and sticks, each driving a control through the same rows every input service uses.
GamepadService.summary: The pad plugs into the computer showing the interface, over USB or Bluetooth, and the browser reports it, so it works on every chip. A fresh service maps the sticks and A onto the first faders and switch.

guide.title: Finding the pad
guide.text:
A browser lists a pad only once a button is pressed with the page open. Chrome and Firefox also need a secure page, which a board's own page is not until marked once.

[Connect a control surface](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonwalk.html#control-surface) has the steps.

guide.title: Learning an input
guide.text: Press learn on a row, then move or press the input to bind. A stick must travel a short way. A pad's first stick positions are rest, so plugging one in off-center moves nothing.

pad.line: The latest pad state the browser wrote: the button bits, then four axes.
pad.more: Each axis rests at 128, its inputs named as SDL's GameController API names them.

inputs.line: The rows: each a button or stick of the standard layout, a learn button and a target.
inputs.more: Assign the surface's controls on the Control card to play a game with the starter rows.

MidiService.line: A MIDI control desk driving the control surface, in the Mackie Control or the Akai APC40 mkII layout.
MidiService.summary:
The desk plugs into the computer showing the interface and the browser reports it. A Mackie desk such as the iCON QCon or the Behringer X-Touch in MC mode works without setup, an Akai APC40 mkII after one choice.

Faders, knobs and SELECT buttons drive the surface, and the desk follows it back with motors, lights and knob rings.

guide.title: Where the desk plugs in
guide.text:
The browser reads a desk on a secure page only: the desktop app's `localhost` is, a board's own page needs marking once. A desk on USB or the network works on any page.

[Connect a control surface](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonwalk.html#control-surface) has the steps.

guide.title: The Akai APC40 mkII
guide.text: Track faders and knobs 1 to 8 move the surface's faders and encoders, and activators flip its switches. The 40 clip pads apply presets 1 to 40: dark when empty, dim white when stored, green when applied.

source.line: Where the desk plugs in: the browser's computer, this USB port, or the network.
source.more: USB needs an S3 with 8 MB of flash or more. The port then carries no serial log or USB flashing, and the board supplies the desk's 5 V.

share.line: Pass the desk on the USB port over the network instead of driving this device.
share.more: The device the desk drives names this one in its `host`. One host at a time.

profile.line: The desk's layout, since each desk lays its controls out in its own messages.
profile.more: Hidden on a shared desk, which the device it is shared with decodes.

host.line: The desk on the network, an address or a name with an optional `:port`.
host.more: Empty waits to be invited, as a Mac's Audio MIDI Setup does. A sharing device announces `<name>.local`.

port.line: The RTP-MIDI port of this device's session.
port.more: Data goes on the port above it.

midi.line: The latest desk messages the browser wrote, in hex.

desk.line: What the desk shows: a message per fader motor, light and knob ring.

hello.line: What the browser sends when the desk connects, such as an APC40's SysEx.

AnalogService.line: A list of ADC pins, each driving a control with a value rather than an event.
AnalogService.summary: The continuous twin of Button, which drives the same controls from a contact. An expression pedal is the shape it is built around.

guide.title: Calibrating a pedal
guide.text: Each row maps the travel between its two raw counts onto the target's own range, so one setup works on any target. A Select with five options takes 0 to 4, and a bool takes on and off. Watch the live raw and value readouts while moving the pedal to each end.

guide.title: Targets
guide.text: A row pointed at a pad does nothing, since a pedal held at 40% has no sensible reading as a preset. Reversed bounds mean inverted. Scripts reach the same pins with `adcRead(pin)` and `adcMax()`, the path for a sensor whose mapping is a condition rather than a range.

smoothing.line: How hard the running average pulls toward each reading, as a percentage.

deadband.line: How far the value must move before the control is written.
deadband.more: Without it a resting pedal rewrites its target fifty times a second.

inputs.line: The pins, each with its raw travel, an invert and a target.

InfraredService.line: An infrared receiver whose learned remote keys drive other modules' controls.
InfraredService.summary: A row is the binding, so a remote with twenty keys has twenty rows. A remote press and an OSC message are indistinguishable to whatever they drive.

guide.title: Learning a key
guide.text: Add a row, press its learn button, then press the remote key: the next code received binds to that row. Learning a key another row holds moves the binding. Pick what the row drives from its target, and whether a press toggles it or nudges it by a value. The status line reports each step.

guide.title: Checking a key
guide.text: The status line says "set pin to receive" until a receiver pin is entered, and shows the code of a key no row holds. On some boards the receiver shares its pin with another peripheral through a board switch.

pin.line: The receiver's GPIO, unset until a board or user enters it.

codes.line: The learned codes, each row binding one remote key to a control.
codes.more: A `set` row is not offered, since a remote reports a press with no release.

MoonLiveService.line: A MoonLive script that reads hardware and drives controls, the input twin of a scripted effect.
MoonLiveService.summary: A mapping row is right for a button and wrong for anything with a condition in it. A script holds state and chooses between outcomes, so a sensor nobody wrote a module for needs a datasheet and eight lines, not a release.

guide.title: Writing the script
guide.text: Everything the script declares appears as a control on the card, and a slider move lands without a recompile. A compile error shows on the status line, and the service does nothing until it is fixed. A script runs on the 50 Hz poll rather than the render tick, so a heavy one costs its own tick.

guide.title: Reading and sending JSON
guide.text: A service reads JSON from the internet with `getJson`, and sends its own documents with `pushJson` to this device or `pushJsonTo` to another. A show builds its own look this way, live and never saved. The calls: [the MoonLive language](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/moonlive.html#json-documents-in-a-service).

script.line: Which `.mls` file to run, picked from the script library.
script.more: Naming a different file recompiles it live. The name is stored, not the text, so a module costs bytes.

FileManagerModule.line: Browse and manage the device filesystem: a folder tree with an inline text editor.
FileManagerModule.summary: Each folder loads its children on first expand. It is distinct from [Filesystem](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/core/system.html#filesystem), the persistence engine that writes the config files this panel shows.

guide.title: Working with files
guide.text:
Click a folder to select it and open or close it, and click a selected file to open the editor. The toolbar acts on the selection: new folder, new file, delete (press twice) and refresh.

Drag files from the desktop onto a folder to upload them.

guide.title: The editor
guide.text: The editor pretty-prints JSON on open and saves atomically. A binary file loads read-only: download it instead.

guide.title: Backup and restore
guide.text: Backup downloads the device's files as one `.json` bundle, and Restore uploads one back. Keep the bundle private: it contains the WiFi password. [Back up and restore a device](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonwalk.html#backup-restore) walks through both.

show hidden.line: Reveal dot-prefixed files and folders, such as `.config`.

flash.line: Flash used and total, as the usage bar.

lastSaved.line: How long ago the configuration was last saved.

SdCardService.line: A board's microSD slot, where one is wired: its wiring, a usage gauge and a format button.
SdCardService.summary: Mounted, its files appear under `/sd`, within the one [FileManager](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/core/system.html#file-manager) tree. This module never duplicates that tree.

guide.title: Mounting
guide.text: Wiring edits apply live, with no reboot. A pulled card is noticed within a second. A missing or unreadable card shows its status instead of retrying: insert the card, then switch the module off and on, edit a pin, or reboot.

guide.title: Formatting
guide.text: The card is FAT32, with 32 KB clusters. A fresh or exFAT card says so on its status, and `format` makes a FAT32 one in place. A large card takes seconds, shown as "formatting", and refuses transfers meanwhile. A Teensy mounts exFAT too, and its format pauses the render.

guide.title: SPI mode
guide.text: Reads hold, but a write over about 50 KB can stop the card until a power cycle. A card mounted that way says so on its status.

board.line: The slot's wiring, from the presets this chip can wire; Custom sets bus and pins.
board.more: P4 SDMMC is the slot every P4 board wires. Classic SDMMC (1-bit) is the Olimex ESP32-Gateway's, Classic SPI the QuinLED Dig-Octa's, and Teensy 4.1 SD socket the Teensy's own slot.

bus.line: The bus under Custom: the SD bus, or the SD spec's SPI mode.

clkPin.line: The clock pin under Custom, SCK in SPI mode.

cmdPin.line: The command pin under Custom, MOSI in SPI mode.

d0Pin.line: Data line 0 under Custom, required, MISO in SPI mode.

d1Pin.line: Data line 1 under Custom; unset with d2 and d3, the bus runs 1-bit.

d2Pin.line: Data line 2 under Custom; unset with d1 and d3, the bus runs 1-bit.

d3Pin.line: Data line 3 under Custom, CS in SPI mode.

pwrPin.line: The pin switching the slot's card power, unset where the slot has none.

format.line: Erase the card and make it FAT32, pressed twice to confirm.

card.line: The card's usage bar, counted in KiB.
card.more: A KiB count keeps a card past 4 GiB reporting correctly: why-the-gauge-counts-kib.

FirmwareUpdateModule.line: Over-the-air firmware flashing: what is installed, and how an install goes.
FirmwareUpdateModule.summary: A flash swaps the binary and restarts the device, the one change that does not apply live. The flash is driven by the web route; the module shows its progress.

guide.title: Two images
guide.text:
A device carrying two images, the app and MoonBase, shows them as two tabs. A Restart in MoonBase button sits on the card.

When MoonBase's version differs from the app's, the card warns and the top bar shows `⬆ MoonBase`; installing the matching one from its tab clears it.

image.line: Which image the card describes, drawn as two tabs.

build.line: The git id, then the build date.

firmware.line: The build variant; on the MoonBase tab, its chip.

partition.line: The installed image against the size of its slot, which a new image must fit.
partition.more: The bar doubles as the install bar: it fills with the incoming image mid-install.

MoonCloudModule.line: The container for everything MoonLight does with a server MoonModules runs.
MoonCloudModule.summary: It holds no settings of its own. Each thing it does is a child with its own consent: [MoonStats](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/core/system.html#stats) reports the install and [MoonTalk](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/core/system.html#talk) is a message board. A user who wants one has not agreed to the other.

outbox.line: The request waiting for the open page to post it.

outbox sent.line: The id of the request the page delivered, which empties the outbox.

MoonStatsModule.line: One opt-in report about this install, sent once per install or upgrade, so development effort goes where the users are.
MoonStatsModule.summary: Off until you answer yes. An upgrade sends one report and a reboot sends nothing.

guide.title: What it sends
guide.text:
The report carries the chip, flash, PSRAM, SDK, device model, memory, light count, and which modules you added. It carries no device name, no addresses, no credentials and no text you typed.

The [privacy policy](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/legal/privacy-policy.html) states what is promised.

consent.more: Nothing is sent and no identifier is computed while it is off.

tests.title: MoonCloud consent is off until asked

reportedVersion.more: It differs from the running version exactly when a report is due.

send update.more: For a setup that changed without a version change. It replaces this install's row rather than adding one.

MoonTalkModule.line: A public message board between MoonLight devices, off until you turn it on.
MoonTalkModule.summary: A child of [MoonCloud](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/core/system.html#mooncloud) with its own consent. A message is sent because you typed one: nothing posts on its own.

guide.title: Public and permanent
guide.text: Everything sent is public and permanent: no private message, no recipient, no delete. There is no authentication, so a sender id can be fabricated by hand.

consent.line: Whether posting and reading are on.
consent.more: Nothing is published or read while it is off.

tests.title: MoonCloud consent is off until asked

shareName.line: Whether your device name rides along, a separate decision.
shareName.more: A device name identifies a person rather than a machine. Without it your messages carry the first 8 characters of your installation id, which groups them without naming you.

message.line: What to say; typing changes nothing on its own.

send.line: Publish the message and clear the box.
send.more: Enter in the message field sends too. The box keeps its text when the server is unreachable.

ImprovProvisioningModule.line: Browser-driven WiFi provisioning over serial: the web installer hands the WiFi credentials to a fresh device.
ImprovProvisioningModule.summary: A freshly flashed board is off your network. Improv carries that first handoff over the cable the browser already used to flash it.

guide.title: Provisioning
guide.text:
[Improv Wi-Fi](https://github.com/improv-wifi) is an open standard, and its sdk-cpp and sdk-js are the specification this implements. Any Improv-capable installer can provision a MoonLight device.

Without a serial link, the device's own access point serves the network instead.

MqttModule.line: Lets a home-automation hub switch the light on and off and set its brightness and color over MQTT.
MqttModule.summary: A small MQTT 3.1.1 client of our own, off until a broker is set, wired by code as a child of Network. Every command goes through the shared control path, so MQTT adds only a transport.

guide.title: Which route
guide.text: Home Assistant finds the device over the WLED integration with no broker. Use MQTT for Homebridge, a broker-only network or another hub. [Home automation](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/reference/home-automation.html#the-mqtt-topics) lists the topics.

guide.title: Getting it connected
guide.text: The status line says why. Give the broker computer's LAN address, never 127.0.0.1, and let port 1883 through its firewall.

broker.line: The broker's hostname or IP address.
broker.more: A hostname such as `homeassistant.lan` is resolved through DNS. On a laptop broker use its LAN address.

password.line: The broker password, stored obfuscated like the WiFi one.

haDiscovery.line: Announce a Home Assistant discovery light, opt-in.
haDiscovery.more: Off by default: Home Assistant already finds the device over the WLED integration, and both would list it twice. Turn it on for broker-only or cross-subnet setups. The firmware update entity follows the same switch.

mqtt_status.line: Where the connection stands, from disabled and idle through connected, or the error.

DevicesModule.line: Discovers other devices on the LAN, MoonLight and WLED among them, and lists them, this one included and marked as such.
DevicesModule.summary: The last-known list survives a reboot. A child of Network, discovery depending on the network being up.

guide.title: Finding WLED devices
guide.text:
WLED lists a device only from the broadcast copy, and the copy costs the rest of the LAN next to nothing.

A network that drops multicast is detected, and the status says so ([IGMP snooping](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/explanation/architecture/moonlight.html#multicast-and-igmp-snooping)).

addressing.line: How presence travels: multicast, or multicast and broadcast.
addressing.more: Broadcast is the default, since WLED devices hear it too.

devices.line: The discovered devices; a row expands to its details.

NetworkModule.line: Brings the device onto the LAN before the HTTP and WebSocket servers start, trying Ethernet, then WiFi, then its own access point.
NetworkModule.summary: Network holds the cascade, its mode and mDNS; each interface's settings are on its own card: Ethernet, WiFi and the access point. A desktop builds the same cards over stubs. The order is described under The cascade in the header.

guide.title: A direct cable to a computer
guide.text:
With no DHCP server on an Ethernet-only build, the device takes a 169.254.x.y address after about 15 seconds. A computer on the same network does too, so open `<name>.local` and set a static address on the Ethernet card.

A DHCP server that appears later still wins.

Firmware MoonBase joins the apps network

mDNS.line: The `<name>.local` hostname, on IPv4 and IPv6.

EthernetModule.line: The wired interface: which board's wiring it uses, and how it gets an address.
EthernetModule.summary: A child of Network, which runs the cascade; it holds what Ethernet needs to join it. It exists where Ethernet is compiled in, and as a developer preview on the desktop.

guide.title: Choosing a static address
guide.text:
Gateway and DNS are optional. A static setting that cannot work, such as a gateway outside the subnet, is not used: the interface keeps DHCP and the card says why.

Changing the addressing of the interface the page reaches the device through asks first, naming where the device will be.

ethBoard.more: Custom shows every pin; a fixed interface has no choice.

ethType.line: The PHY chip, seeded per chip and overridden by the catalog.

ethPhyAddr.line: The PHY's address on the management bus.
ethPhyAddr.more: -1 scans for it. Signed rather than a GPIO, so the auto-detect sentinel round-trips.

ethClockExtIn.line: Whether the clock comes into the chip rather than out of it.

WiFiModule.line: The WiFi station: the networks the device knows, in the order it prefers them, and the radio's settings.
WiFiModule.summary: A child of Network, which runs the cascade; it holds what joining WiFi needs. Joining is connect-first, as on a phone: tap a network in range, type its password, Connect.

guide.title: The order of joining
guide.text: The device tries the known networks in priority order, ten seconds each to join, and opens its access point after the last. Networks a scan in the last five minutes did not see go to the end of that order. Each network keeps its own IP settings.

guide.title: Connecting
guide.text: Connect joins a network at once. A network picked from those in range is saved only once it joined, and "incorrect password" says why when it did not.

address.line: Where to reach the device on its new network, by address.
address.more: It shows after a join from the access point. Open the link in a browser, since a phone's sign-in screen has no address bar.

tests.title: AccessPoint first setup from its own network

scan.line: Look for the networks in range.
scan.more: A scan takes the radio off-channel for a few seconds, which drops incoming lights while connected. The device scans by itself only when its access point opens.

scanned.line: How long ago the last scan finished.

available.line: The networks in range; Connect joins one now.
available.more: Tap a network, type its password, Connect. A join from the access point shows the device's `.local` link on the row first, since the phone often lands back on its own network.

known.line: The networks it joins, in priority order.
known.more: Each has its name, password and IP settings. A Static setting that cannot work joins by DHCP, with the reason on its row. Editing the addressing of the network the page arrives through asks first.

rssi.line: The signal strength of the joined network.

txPower.line: The power the radio transmits at now.

txPowerSetting.line: Caps the radio's transmit power, for a board that browns out.
txPowerSetting.more: 0 lifts the cap. Lower it when the board resets as the radio sends.

AccessPointModule.line: The device's own WiFi network, at `4.3.2.1`: joining it opens the UI by itself, as a sign-in screen.
AccessPointModule.summary:
A child of Network, which opens and closes it; `http://4.3.2.1` reaches the UI as well.

The first known WiFi network's password protects it, so it is open only on a first setup or with an open home network. Its clients receive no stored password or config file.

guide.title: Getting back in
guide.text: Switch the device on and off four times, each within a few seconds, and it opens for that boot without a password, whatever its setting says. That boot runs in safe mode: the way back to a device whose router changed, with every setting kept.

guide.title: After a join from the access point
guide.text:
A join asked for from a phone keeps the access point up beside the new network for two minutes, and the WiFi card shows the device's links.

Joining moves the radio to the router's channel, which knocks the phone off, so open a link in the browser: the sign-in screen has no address bar.

opens.line: When it opens: on failure, always, or first setup only.
opens.more: A join in progress holds it back, since one radio serves both; first setup stays open until a network or Ethernet is set.

name.line: The network name: `MM-` and four MAC digits.
name.more: Anonymous, so the air does not say whose device it is.

FilesystemModule.line: The persistence engine: it writes control values to `/.config/*.json` and restores them on boot, so settings survive a reboot.
FilesystemModule.summary: It is always loaded and runs first, so its load hook fires before any other module sets up. File Manager browses the stored files.

light/modifiers.md.title: Modifiers
light/modifiers.md.line: A modifier sits between an [effect](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/effects.html) and the output: it reshapes where the pixels land, or masks them, without changing what the effect draws.
light/modifiers.md.summary:
Modifiers compose: a [Layer](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/supporting.html#layer) applies its whole stack in child order, each reshaping the result of the one below. A static modifier is baked into the layer's mapping at rebuild. A dynamic one also runs a pass every frame, and an animated one rebuilds its static fold on its own clock.

A modifier folds coordinates rather than drawing, so it uses little of the shared [power functions](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/power-functions.html). Each card's emoji are its tags, as the [tag emoji legend](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/explanation/architecture/index.html#tag-emoji-legend) explains.

light/layouts.md.title: Layouts
light/layouts.md.line: A layout says where the lights physically are: it maps each light's index to an (x, y, z) position, the shape an [effect](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/effects.html) draws onto and a [driver](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html) sends out.
light/layouts.md.summary:
The [Layouts](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/supporting.html#layouts) container holds one or more layouts and composes them into one coordinate space, which a [Layer](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/supporting.html#layer) renders over. The container itself takes no controls.

Each card's emoji are its tags, as the [tag emoji legend](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/explanation/architecture/index.html#tag-emoji-legend) explains.

videos.caption: Layouts: a grid, a ring, a spiral, a cube, tubes, and two written in MoonLive.

light/effects.md.title: Effects
light/effects.md.line: An effect draws: each frame it writes a color per light into its [Layer](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/supporting.html#layer)'s buffer, which modifiers reshape and a driver sends out.
light/effects.md.summary:
Effects are built from the shared [power functions](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/power-functions.html), the drawing, field and motion routines every effect composes. One that names an index color reads the global palette, the `palette` control on [Drivers](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/supporting.html#drivers).

Each card's emoji are its tags, as the [tag emoji legend](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/explanation/architecture/index.html#tag-emoji-legend) explains, and its dimension is its native axes: a Layer extrudes a lower-dimensional effect onto a bigger grid.

light/drivers.md.title: Drivers
light/drivers.md.line: A driver sends the lights out: to LEDs on a wire, a HUB75 panel, the network, a smart-light bridge or the web UI.
light/drivers.md.summary: Each reads its own slice of the [Drivers](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/supporting.html#drivers) container's buffer through the shared window controls. A physical output corrects it through the shared correction controls, while [Preview](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/moonmodules/light/drivers.html#preview) shows it as it is. A card's emoji are its [tags](https://moonmodules.org/MoonLight/explanation/architecture/index.html#tag-emoji-legend).

videos.caption: Drivers on a desktop: preview, NDI, RTSP, HLS, network send and Hue.
Drivers on a device: RMT and parallel LED pins, HUB75, panel cards, and the network senders.

core/services.md.title: Services
core/services.md.line: The container for the user-added Service modules, the capability bridges a device provides or consumes.
core/services.md.summary: A service is added and removed at runtime, the core twin of the light domain's Effects and Drivers. Fixed device infrastructure, such as identity and network, lives under System.

videos.caption: Every service in turn: audio, button, analog, infrared, and a scripted one.
